The one who is nursing (murdi') is a woman who has a child she is nursing, and the nursing woman (murda'ah) is one who has put the breast to the infant's mouth.

On this basis, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from what she was nursing﴾ is more eloquent than "murdi'" in this context. For a woman may be distracted from a baby when she is not directly nursing it; but when she has taken the breast to its mouth and is occupied with nursing it, she is not distracted from it except by a matter greater in her eyes than occupation with nursing.

Reflect, may Allah have mercy on you, on the wondrous secret in His, glorified is He, turning away from "every pregnant one" (kullu hamil) to His saying: ﴿with every pregnancy (dhāt ḥaml)﴾. For the word "hāmil" may be applied both to one who is prepared for pregnancy and to one who is at the beginning of her pregnancy and its earliest stages.

So when it is said "dhāt ḥaml," it refers only to one whose pregnancy has become apparent and who is fit to deliver, whether the child is fully formed or a miscarriage, just as one says "dhāt walad."

Thus, for "murda'ah" He used the feminine ending (tā’), which confirms the act of nursing itself and not merely readiness for it, while for "ḥāmil" He used the descriptor that confirms the existence of the pregnancy and its readiness for delivery. And Allah knows best.

He, glory be to Him, says: If you are in doubt about the resurrection (al-Ba'th), then you do not doubt that you are created, nor do you doubt the beginning of your creation, passing from one state to another until the time of death. The resurrection that you were promised is the likeness of the first creation (al-Nash'a al-Ula). The two are alike in possibility and in occurrence. Your being brought back after death as a new creation is like the first creation, about which you have no doubt. So how do you deny one of the two creations when you witness its like?

He, glory be to Him, repeated this meaning and expressed it in His Book in the most concise, most indicative, clearest, most decisive in cutting off excuses, and most binding in proof phrases, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you considered what you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creators? We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 58-60]. ﴿In order that We may substitute your likenesses and produce you in what you do not know﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 61]. ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation, so why do you not remember?﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 62]. So He pointed them, through the first creation, to the second, and showed that if they reflected, they would know that there is no difference between the two in the power's relation to each of them. He, glory be to Him, also combined the two creations in His saying: ﴿And that He created the two mates, the male and the female (45), from a sperm-drop when it is emitted (46), and that upon Him is the other creation (47)﴾ [al-Najm: 45-47].

And in His saying: ﴿Did he not used to be a sperm-drop emitted (37), then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ [al-Qiyama: 37-40].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and grows from every beautiful pair (5). That is because Allah is the Truth, and it is He who gives life to the dead, and it is He who is over all things competent (6). And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves (7)﴾ [al-Hajj: 5-7].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who gives it life is the one who will give life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾ [Fussilat: 39].

Allah, glory be to Him, made the reviving of the earth after its death a likeness of the reviving of the dead, and the bringing forth of plants from it a likeness of their being brought out of the graves. Through the likeness He pointed to its counterpart, and He made this a sign and an evidence for five objectives:

First: the existence of the Creator, that He is the manifest Truth. This necessitates affirming the attributes of His perfection: His power, His will, His life, His knowledge, His wisdom, His mercy, and His acts.

Second: that He gives life to the dead.

Third: the generality of His power over all things.

Fourth: the coming of the Hour, and that there is no doubt about it.

Fifth: that He brings the dead out of the graves just as He brings out plants from the earth.

He, glory be to Him, has repeated the mention of this proof in His Book many times, because its premises are sound, its indication is clear, its subject is near, and it is far from every objection and doubt, and because He made it an insight and a reminder, as He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And the earth—We have spread it out, cast into it firm mountains, and caused to grow in it from every beautiful pair (7), as an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾.

**(A subtle point)**

He said in Surah al-Hajj: ﴿Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associate others with God — indeed God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed God is Witness over all things.﴾ He did not say here, "whoever among them believes in God and the Last Day," because He mentioned with them "the Magians and those who associate others with God." So He mentioned six communities, two of which are wretched, and four of which are divided into wretched and blessed. Where He promised reward to the people of faith and righteous deeds among them, He mentioned only four communities, and nothing more.

In the verse on the separation of the communities, He included the two communities with them. In the verse on the promise of recompense, He did not include them. So it is known that the Sabians include the believer and the disbeliever, the wretched and the blessed. This is an ancient community, older than the Jews and the Christians, and they are of several kinds: Sabians who are upright monotheists (hunafa'), and Sabians who are polytheists.

**(Section)**

He mentioned the two communities that have no scripture and are not divided into wretched and blessed, namely the Magians and the polytheists, in the verse of separation, and He did not mention them in the verse of the promise of Paradise.

He mentioned the Sabians along with them, so it is known that among them are the wretched and the blessed.

These were the people of Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), and they were the people of his call. They were in Harran, which is the home of the Sabians.

They were of two kinds: Sabians who were upright monotheists, and Sabians who were polytheists. The polytheists among them venerated the seven planets and the twelve zodiac signs, and depicted them in their temples.

For those heavenly bodies they had special temples, which were their great places of worship, like churches for the Christians and synagogues for the Jews.

They had a great temple for the Sun, a temple for the Moon, a temple for Venus, a temple for Jupiter, a temple for Mars, a temple for Mercury, a temple for Saturn, and a temple for the First Cause.

For these heavenly bodies they had special acts of worship and supplications. They depicted them in those temples, took idols specific to each of them, and offered sacrifices to them. They had five prayers in the day and night, similar to the prayers of the Muslims.

Groups among them fasted the month of Ramadan, faced the Ka'bah in their prayers, venerated Mecca, regarded pilgrimage to it as obligatory, forbade carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine, and forbade in marriage the same degrees of kinship that the Muslims forbid.

On this doctrine was a group of notables of the state in Baghdad, among them Hilal ibn al-Muhassin al-Sabi, the head of the chancery (diwan al-insha') and the author of the well-known epistles. He fasted with the Muslims, celebrated the festivals with them, paid zakat, and avoided what is forbidden.

People were amazed at his agreement with the Muslims, although he was not upon their religion.

The root of this religion of theirs, as they claimed, is that they adopt the best of the religions and doctrines of the world, and withdraw from the ugliness of what they are upon, in speech and in action. For this reason they were called Sabians, meaning "those who depart" (khariji). They departed from being bound to the whole of any religion and its details, except what they saw in it as truth.

The Quraysh disbelievers used to call the Prophet (ﷺ) "the Sabian," and his companions "the Sabi'ah." It is said: sabi'a al-rajul (with the hamza), when a man departed from one thing to another. And sabā yasbū means he inclined, and from it is His saying:

﴿And unless You turn away their scheming from me, I shall incline toward them﴾ [Yusuf: 33], meaning I shall yearn for them.

The hamzated and the weak-lettered forms share a meaning. The hamzated form means turning away from a thing; the weak-lettered form means inclining toward it. The active participle from the hamzated form is ṣābi' (صابئ), on the pattern of qāri' (قارئ); from the weak-lettered form it is ṣāb (صاب), on the pattern of qāḍi (قاض). The plural of the first is ṣābi'ūn (صابئون), like qāri'ūn; the plural of the second is ṣābūn (صابون), like qāḍūn. Both have been read in recitation.

The point is that this community shared with all the nations and also separated from them. Its upright monotheists shared with the people of Islam in upright monotheism (hanifiyyah). Its polytheists shared with the worshippers of idols, and considered themselves to be upon the right course.

Most of this community are philosophers. The philosophers, by their own claim, take from every religion the best of what reason indicates. Their rational ones require following the prophets and their laws. Some of them neither require nor forbid that. Their fools and riffraff forbid it, as the mention of Satan's manipulation of them will come after this.

For this reason, these philosophers and the Sabians were not among the independent nations that have a scripture and a prophet, although they were among the people of the prophets' call.

No nation has ever existed to which God, glory be to Him, has not established His proof and cut off their excuse:

﴿So that people will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165], and His proof will be against them.

The point is that the Sabians are sects: upright-monotheist Sabians, polytheist Sabians, philosopher Sabians, and Sabians who take the best of what the adherents of the religions and sects hold, without being bound to any religion or sect.

Then among them are those who affirm prophethood in general and hesitate about its details; among them are those who affirm it in general and in detail; and among them are those who deny it in general and in detail.

They all affirm that the world has a Maker, a Originator, All-Wise, exalted above defects and imperfections.

Then the polytheists among them said: "We have no way to reach His majesty except through intermediaries."

So it is incumbent on us to draw near to Him through the mediation of the spiritual beings nearest to Him. These are the spiritual, brought-near beings, sanctified from material substances and bodily powers; indeed they are created upon purity. We draw near to them, and through them we draw near to Him. They are our lords, our gods, and our intercessors with the Lord of lords and the God of gods. We worship them only so that they may bring us near to God in closeness.

So it is incumbent on us to purify our souls from natural desires, and refine our characters from the attachments of the irascible powers, until a correspondence arises between us and the spiritual beings, and our spirits connect with them. Then we ask them for our needs, present our conditions to them, and turn to them in all our affairs, and they intercede for us with our God and their God.

This purification and refinement is only achieved by drawing aid from the spiritual beings, through humbling oneself and supplicating with invocations: prayers, almsgiving, slaughtering sacrifices, incense, and incantations. Then our souls acquire readiness and aid without the intermediary of the messengers; rather we take from the same source from which the messengers took. Thus our judgment and their judgment will be one, and we and they will be in one rank.

They said: "The prophets are like us in kind, our partners in substance, and our likenesses in form. They eat what we eat and drink what we drink. They are only humans like us, wishing to make themselves superior to us."

The Ittihadiyyah (the monists of unity of existence), the followers of Ibn 'Arabi, Ibn Sab'in, al-'Afif al-Tilimsani, and their likes, went further than these people with what the leader of their sect, Muhammad ibn 'Arabi, said: that the saint (wali) is higher in rank than the messenger, because he takes from the same source from which the angel who reveals to the messenger takes; so he is higher than him by two degrees.

Thus these heretics placed themselves and their shaykhs two degrees above the messengers in receiving, while their brothers among the polytheists did not place themselves above the prophets in that reception; they regarded themselves as being in the rank of the prophets, and did not claim to be above them.

The point is that these people disbelieved in the two foundations which all the messengers and prophets, from the first of them to the last, brought:

The first: worshipping God alone, without partner, and rejecting whatever is worshipped besides Him as a god.

The second: believing in His messengers and in what they brought from God, by affirmation, acknowledgment, submission, and obedience.

This is not peculiar to the polytheist Sabians, as many writers of doctrines have erred in claiming; rather this is the doctrine of the polytheists of all nations. But the polytheism of the Sabians was from the direction of the stars and the celestial beings. For this reason, the leader of the upright monotheists, upon whom be the blessings and peace of God, debated them about the invalidity of their divinity, with the best and clearest debate that God, glory be to Him, related in Surah al-An'am [74–83]; in it his argument became manifest and their argument was refuted.

He said, after showing the invalidity of the divinity of the stars, the moon, and the sun by their setting, and that it is not fitting for God to disappear and set, but He must be ever-present and not absent, just as He must be dominant and irresistible, not overcome or subdued; beneficial to His worshippers, able to grant them harm and benefit, hearing their speech, seeing their place, guiding them, directing them, and warding off from them everything that harms and injures them. This belongs to God alone. So every deity besides Him is false.

When the leader of the upright monotheists saw that the sun, the moon, and the stars were not in this station, he rose from them to their Originator, Creator, and Maker, and said:

﴿Indeed I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth, as an upright monotheist﴾ [al-An'am: 79].

In this there is an indication that He, glory be to Him, is the Creator of their places and their stations, on which they depend, and without which they have no subsistence. They need a place in which to subsist, and an Originator who creates, governs, and nurtures them. What is needy, created, nurtured, and governed cannot be a god. His people argued with him about God, and whoever argues about the worship of God, his argument is void.

Abraham, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Do you argue with me about God when He has guided me?﴾ [al-An'am: 80].

**[Issue: The questioner's statement: "It is well known among you that the People of the Two Books were prevented from entering Islam only by leadership and worldly gain, and nothing else." This is the speech of one ignorant of what the Muslims hold and what the disbelievers hold.]**

As for the Muslims, they have not said that nothing prevented the People of the Book from entering Islam except leadership and worldly gain alone. If some of their common folk said this, it does not bind their scholars as a body. Those among the People of the Two Books and others who refused to enter Islam are a very small portion relative to those who entered it from among them. Indeed, most of the nations entered Islam willingly, by desire and choice, not by compulsion and constraint.

God, glory be to Him and exalted, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger to the people of the earth, and they were five categories who had spread over the earth: Jews, Christians, Magians, Sabians, and polytheists.

These are the categories that had gained control over the world from its east to its west.

As for the Jews, most of them were in Yemen, Khaybar, Medina, and what surrounds them. On the borders of Syria they were humiliated along with the Christians, and some of them in the land of Persia were humiliated along with the Magians, and a group of them was in the land of the Maghrib. They were most powerful in Medina, Khaybar, and their surroundings. God, glory be to Him and exalted, had dispersed them into nations throughout the earth and stripped them of dominion and honor.

As for the Christians, they were spread across the earth: all of Syria was Christian; the land of the Maghrib was predominantly Christian; likewise Egypt, Abyssinia, Nubia, al-Jazirah, Mosul, the land of Najran, and other lands.

As for the Magians, they were the people of the kingdom of Persia and what was connected to it.

As for the Sabians, they were the people of Harran and much of the lands of Rome.

As for the polytheists, they were the whole of the Arabian Peninsula, the lands of India, the lands of the Turks, and what bordered them.

The religions of the people of the earth do not go beyond these five religions, and the religion of the upright monotheists is not known among them at all. And these five religions are all for Satan, as Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, and others said: "The religions are six: one for the Merciful and five for Satan."

These six religions are mentioned in the verse of separation, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associate others with God — indeed God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed God is Witness over all things.﴾

When God sent His Messenger (ﷺ), most of the people of these religions responded to him, and to his successors after him, willingly and by choice. He never compelled anyone to religion. He fought only those who fought against him and waged war upon him. As for those who made peace with him and entered into a truce, he did not fight them and did not compel them to enter his religion, in obedience to the command of his Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, when He says: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become distinct from error﴾.

This is a negation with the meaning of a prohibition: that is, do not compel anyone in religion. This verse was revealed concerning men among the Companions who had sons who had become Jews and Christians before Islam. When Islam came, the fathers embraced Islam and wanted to compel the sons to religion, so God, glory be to Him and exalted, forbade them from that, until they themselves would be the ones who choose to enter Islam.

The correct view is that the verse is general in regard to every disbeliever. This is evident according to the view of those who permit taking the jizyah (poll tax) from all disbelievers; they are not compelled to enter the religion, but either they enter the religion or they pay the jizyah, as the people of Iraq and the people of Medina hold, even though these scholars excepted some idol-worshippers.

Whoever reflects upon the biography of the Prophet (ﷺ) will see clearly that he never compelled anyone to his religion at all, and that he fought only those who fought him. As for those who made a truce with him, he did not fight them as long as they remained upon their truce and did not break their covenant. Rather, God, exalted is He, commanded him to keep faith with them as long as they remained upright toward him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them﴾.

When he came to Medina, he made peace with the Jews and left them upon their religion. When they fought against him, broke his covenant, and initiated hostilities, he fought them: he showed favor to some of them, expelled some of them, and fought some of them.

Likewise, when he made a truce with the Quraysh for ten years, he did not initiate fighting against them until they themselves began fighting him and breaking his covenant. Then he campaigned against them in their own lands. Before that, they had been attacking him, as they marched against him on the day of the Trench, and on the day of Badr too they came to fight him. Had they turned away from him, he would not have fought them.

The purpose is that he (ﷺ) never compelled anyone at all to enter his religion. People entered his religion by choice and willingly. Most of the people of the earth entered his call once guidance became clear to them and they recognised that he was truly the Messenger of Allah. Thus the people of Yemen were upon Judaism, and most of them were, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Mu'adh when he sent him to Yemen: "You are going to a people who have a Book, so let the first thing you call them to be the testimony that there is no god but Allah," and he mentioned the hadith. Then they entered Islam without desire or fear. Likewise were those of the Jews of Madinah who embraced Islam, who were many groups, other than Abdullah (ibn Salam), mentioned in the books of biography (al-Sirah) and the military campaigns (al-Maghazi). They did not embrace Islam out of desire for worldly gain or fear of the sword. Rather, they embraced it in a time of the Muslims' need, the multitude of their enemies, and the hostility of the people of the earth towards them, without whip or cord. They bore the enmity of their relatives and being deprived by them of benefit in wealth and person, despite the weakness of the Muslims' might and the scarcity of their means. One of them would oppose his father, his mother, his household and his clan, and would leave this world out of desire for Islam, not for leadership or wealth. Rather, he would divest himself of leadership and wealth, and would bear the harm of the disbelievers, from their beating and insulting him and their various kinds of harm, and that would not divert him from his religion.

If many of the rabbis (ahbar), the monks (ruhban) and the priests (qissisin), and whoever this questioner has mentioned, have chosen disbelief, then most of the people of the earth from the groups of disbelievers have embraced Islam, and only a minority remains compared to those who embraced it. Thus the Christians of Syria (al-Sham) were filling Syria, then they became Muslims except for a rare few, so they became among the Muslims like a black hair on a white bull.

Likewise the Magians (al-Majus) were a nation whose number none but Allah the Exalted can count, yet they unanimously embraced Islam, and only a rare few remained behind. The lands became lands of Islam, and whoever of them did not embrace Islam came under the jizya (poll tax) and humiliation. Likewise the Jews: most of them embraced Islam, and there remained only a small scattered remnant in the lands.

So the saying of this ignorant one, that these two nations, whose number none but Allah the Exalted can count, disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), is manifest falsehood and clear slander. Even if they had all unanimously chosen disbelief, they would be like the people of Noah in that, and Noah (ﷺ) remained among them for nine hundred and fifty years, calling them to Allah the Exalted and showing them signs that establish Allah's proof against them, yet they unanimously disbelieved except for a few of them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few.﴾

They were many times more numerous than these two disbelieving nations, the people of wrath and the people of misguidance. The people of 'Ad unanimously disbelieved, and they were a great nation, intelligent, until they were uprooted by punishment. The people of Thamud all unanimously disbelieved after seeing the great sign of the kind by which humans believe, and despite this they chose disbelief over belief, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance.﴾ And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud—it has become clear to you from their dwellings. And Satan made their deeds appealing to them and barred them from the way, though they were discerning.﴾

These are two great nations, among the greatest of nations, who unanimously disbelieved while having insight. So when the nations of wrath and misguidance unanimously disbelieve, that is no novelty. And these are the people of Pharaoh, despite their multitude, who unanimously denied the prophethood of Musa, peace be upon him, despite the clear signs appearing one after another, and none of them believed except one man who was concealing his faith.

Also, it is said to the Christians: these Jews, despite their multitude at the time of the Messiah, peace be upon him, to the extent that they had filled the lands of Syria, as Allah the Exalted said: {And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed}, and they unanimously denied the Messiah and rejected his prophethood, and among them were the rabbis, the monks, the worshippers and the scholars, until only the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) believed in him. So if it was permissible for the Jews, among whom were the rabbis, the worshippers, the ascetics and others, to unanimously reject the prophethood of the Messiah and disbelieve in him despite the manifest signs of his truthfulness like the sun, then it was permissible for them to deny the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). And it is known that the permissibility of that for the nation of misguidance, who are more astray than cattle, namely the Christians, is more fitting and more worthy.

So this question that this questioner has raised applies exactly to every prophet whom a nation has denied. If this questioner holds that all those nations were right, then he has disbelieved in all the Messengers. And if he says: the prophets were upon the truth, and those nations, despite their multitude and the abundance of their intellects, were upon falsehood, then the deniers of Muhammad (ﷺ), who are the fewest and the most despicable of these groups, are even more fitting and more worthy of being upon falsehood. And whichever nation you consider, you will find that the believers in the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) are its majority, while the least and most despicable of it are those who deny his prophethood. The expanse of Islam has spread across the eastern and western parts of the earth to the utmost extent by these nations entering his religion and affirming his message, and there remained those of each nation who did not enter his religion, and they are the least of each nation.

Where do the Christians who deny his message today stand in relation to the nation of Christianity that existed before him?!

Likewise the Jews, the Magians and the Sabians have no proportion, compared to those who deny his message after his mission, to the whole of that nation before his mission.

Allah the Exalted has informed about the nations who unanimously denied the messengers and whom Allah destroyed. He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him, so We made them follow one another and made them as tales. So away with a people who do not believe.﴾

So He informed about these nations that they agreed in denying their messengers, and that He annihilated them all. And He said: ﴿Thus, no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A magician or a madman." Did they charge one another with it? Rather, they are a transgressing people.﴾

It is certain that Allah the Exalted did not destroy these many nations except after guidance had become clear to them, and they chose disbelief over it. Had guidance not become clear to them and they had chosen otherwise, they would not have been destroyed, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We would not destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers.﴾ And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So why was there not a town that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time.﴾

That is, there was no town that believed and its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus. And it is certain that no prophet from the first of them to the last was believed, nor was any nation's following of him as great as the following of Muhammad ibn Abdullah (ﷺ) was.

Those from the nations who followed him are many times more numerous than these two nations that denied, a number none but Allah can count. And no one who has even a little measure of intellect doubts that misguidance, ignorance, error and corruption of intellect are closer to those who oppose him and deny his prophethood than to those who affirm his prophethood.

Then it is said: how is it permissible for these nations, whom none but Allah can count, who have reached the eastern and western parts of the earth, despite the differences of their natures, their aims and the divergence of their purposes, to unanimously follow one who lies about Allah and about reason, makes lawful what Allah and His messengers have forbidden, and forbids what He has made lawful? And it is known that the one who lies about Allah the Exalted in claiming prophethood is the worst of Allah's creation, the most wicked, the most unjust and the most lying.

And no one with even the least intellect doubts that the unanimity of most nations in following this Prophet (ﷺ), leaving their homelands and wealth, opposing their fathers and clans in following him, and offering their souls before him, is among the most impossible of impossibilities.

Therefore, to permit the choice of disbelief after guidance has become clear, by a small, despicable remnant having many aims from these two nations, is more fitting than permitting it for the Muslims who have spread across the eastern and western parts of the earth, and who are the most intelligent of nations and the most complete in all qualities of virtue. Where are the intellects of the worshippers of the calf and the worshippers of the cross, whose conduct made all other intelligent people laugh at their intellects, and who showed them the extent of their intellects by what they said about their object of worship, compared to the intellects of the Muslims?

And if it is permissible for a nation, among whom is one like this questioner mentioned, to agree that the Lord of the worlds and Creator of the heavens and the earths descended from the throne of His majesty and the footstool of His exaltation, and entered the belly of a woman in the place of menstruation and bleeding for several months, then came out from her womb as an infant sucking the breast, crying and growing little by little, eating and drinking, urinating and being healthy and falling ill, rejoicing and grieving, giving birth and suffering pain; then He devised a stratagem against His enemy Iblis by enabling His enemies, the Jews, over Himself, so they seized Him and drove Him to two pieces of wood on which they would crucify Him, while they dragged Him to the cross, with the rabble and the base before Him, behind Him, to His right and to His left, while He was crying out for help and weeping; they brought Him close to the two pieces of wood, then they crowned Him with a crown of thorns, slapped Him with slaps, then carried Him onto the cross, nailed His hands and feet, and placed Him between two thieves, and He is the One who chose all this so that the stratagem against Iblis might be complete, to free Adam and all the prophets from his prison, so He ransomed them with Himself until they were freed from the prison of Iblis.

Then if it is permissible for this nation to agree, among whom are the rabbis, the monks, the priests, the ascetics, the worshippers, the jurists and those I have mentioned, upon this saying about their object of worship and their god, to the extent that one of them, who is among their great ones, said: the hand that created Adam is the one that touched the nails and suffered the crucifixion; then how is it permissible for them to agree upon denying the one who came to declare them disbelievers and misguided, who proclaimed openly and secretly their lying about Allah the Exalted, their cursing Him with the most vile curses, their lying about the Messiah, their altering his religion, who opposed and fought them and disassociated himself from them and from the Messiah, and who informed that they are the fuel of the fire and the pebbles of Hell? This is one of the reasons for which they chose disbelief over belief, and it is among the greatest reasons.

Your saying that the Muslims claim that nothing prevented them from entering Islam except leadership and the meal, and nothing else, is a lie against the Muslims. Rather, leadership and the meal are among the reasons that prevent them from entering the religion. We and others have debated a group of them, and when the corruption of what they were upon became clear to some of them, they said: "If we entered Islam we would be among the least of Muslims, of no account, while we now dominate the people of our religion in their wealth and positions, and have the greatest standing among them!" And did anything prevent Pharaoh and his people from following Musa except that?!

The reasons that prevent acceptance of the truth are very numerous. Among them is ignorance of it, and this is the reason that prevails over most souls, for whoever is ignorant of something opposes it and opposes its people. If hatred for the one who commands him with the truth, his enmity towards him and his envy are added to this reason, the obstacle to acceptance becomes stronger. If his habit, his custom, and his upbringing upon what his fathers were upon, and what those he loves and respects were upon, are added to that, the obstacle grows stronger. If he further imagines that the truth to which he is called will come between him and his status, his honour, his desires and his aims, the obstacle to acceptance becomes exceedingly strong.

If fear of his companions, his clan and his people for his own self, his wealth and his status is added to that, as happened to Heraclius, king of the Christians in Syria, in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the obstacle to accepting the truth increases in strength. For Heraclius recognised the truth and resolved to enter Islam, but his people did not obey him and he feared them for his own self, so he chose disbelief over Islam after guidance had become clear to him, as the story of him will come, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Ibn al-Qayyim, *al-Tafsir al-Qayyim*, on Surah 22, verse 17 (part 3 of 4)

Among the greatest of these causes is **envy** (*hasad*). It is a disease hidden in the soul. The envier sees the one he envies given preference over him and granted what others were not granted, so envy does not let him submit to that person or become one of his followers. Did anything prevent Iblis from prostrating to Adam except envy? When he saw Adam preferred over him and raised above him, he choked on his own saliva, and he chose disbelief over faith after having been among the angels.

This disease also prevented the Jews from believing in ʿIsa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary). They knew with certain knowledge that he was a Messenger of God who came with clear proofs and guidance, yet envy led them to choose disbelief over faith, and they unanimously rejected him. They were a nation that included rabbis, scholars, ascetics, judges, kings, and rulers.

Moreover, al-Masih (the Messiah) came with the ruling of the Tawrah (Torah). He brought no law (*shariʿah*, divine law) that contradicted it and he did not fight them. He only came to make lawful some things that had been forbidden to them, as a lightening, mercy, and kindness, and he came to complete the Tawrah's law. Despite this, they all chose disbelief over faith. How, then, would their state be with a Prophet who came with an independent law (*shariʿah*) that abrogates (*nasikhah*) all previous laws, who rebuked them for their ugly deeds, publicized their disgraces, and expelled them from their homes? They fought and waged war against him, yet in all of that he was victorious over them, prevailed over them, and he and his companions rose above them, while they remained constantly in lowliness. How, then, would envy and rebellion not control their hearts? Where does their state with him stand in comparison to their state with al-Masih, when they rejected him after guidance had become clear to them? This cause alone is sufficient to reject the truth. How much more so when the loss of leadership and of worldly gains is added to it, as was mentioned earlier?

Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who was the son of Abu Jahl's sister, said: "O uncle, did you accuse Muhammad of lying before he said what he said?" He replied: "O nephew! By God, Muhammad was truthful among us when he was young, and he was called *al-Amin* (the Trustworthy). We never found him to have lied at all." He said: "O uncle! Then why do you not follow him?" He replied: "O nephew! We and the Banu Hashim competed for honor. They fed and we fed, they gave drink and we gave drink, they gave protection and we gave protection. Then, when we knelt together on our knees, like two horses in a race, they said: 'Among us is a Prophet. When will we attain the like of this?'"

Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq said on the day of Badr to Abu Jahl: "O Abu al-Hakam! Tell me about Muhammad: is he truthful or a liar? No one of Quraysh is here except you and me, and no one hears our conversation." Abu Jahl replied: "Woe to you! By God, Muhammad is truly truthful, and Muhammad has never lied. But when the Banu Qusayy take the banner, the custody of the Ka'bah, the watering of the pilgrims, and the prophethood, what will remain for the rest of Quraysh?"

As for the Jews, their scholars knew him just as they knew their own sons. Ibn Ishaq said: "ʿAsim ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, from Qatadah, from a shaykh of the Banu Qurayzah, who said: 'Do you know how Asad and Thaʿlabah, the two sons of Suʿyah, and Asad ibn ʿUbayd became Muslims? They were not of the Banu Qurayzah or the Banu al-Nadir; they were above that.'" I said: "No." He said: "A man from among the Jews of al-Sham came to us named Ibn al-Hayban, and he stayed with us. By God, we never saw a man who prayed the five prayers better than him. He came to us two years before the mission of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Whenever we were struck by drought and rain was scarce, we would say: 'O Ibn al-Hayban, go out and pray for rain for us.' He would reply: 'No, by God, not until you bring forward a charity before you leave.' We would ask: 'How much?' He would say: 'A sa' of dates, or two mudd of barley.' We would give it, then he would go out to the outskirts of our lava field, and we would go out with him to ask for rain. By God, he would not rise from his place until we were rained upon and ran through the mountain paths. He did this once, twice, and three times. When his death approached, we gathered around him, and he said: 'O assembly of Jews! Do you see what has driven me out of the land of wine and dates to the land of misery and hunger?' They said: 'You know best.' He said: 'I only left to await the coming of a Prophet whose time has drawn near. This land is his place of emigration. Follow him, and do not let anyone precede you to him when he emerges. O assembly of Jews, he will be sent with the shedding of blood and the taking of captives, women and children, from among those who oppose him. Do not let that deter you from him.' Then he died. When the night came on which Qurayzah was conquered, those three young men, who were youths and boys, said: 'O assembly of Jews, this is the one whom Ibn al-Hayban described to you.' They said: 'He is not him.' They replied: 'Yes, by God, he has his attributes.' Then they came down and became Muslims, and they left their wealth and families behind."

Ibn Ishaq said: "Their wealth was in the fortress with the polytheists, and when it was conquered, it was returned to them."

Ibn Ishaq also said: "Salih ibn Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf narrated to me, from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: 'Among our sons there was a Jew who went out one morning to the assembly of his people, the Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal, and he spoke about the resurrection, the Day of Judgment, Paradise and Hell, the reckoning, and the Balance. He said this to people of idolatry who did not believe that there would be any resurrection after death. This was before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ). They said: "Woe to you, so-and-so! Will this really happen, that people will be raised after their death to your abode, in which there is Paradise and Hell, and they will be recompensed for their deeds?" He said: "Yes, by Him by whom oaths are sworn, I wish that my share of that Fire would be that you light the greatest oven in your house, heat it, then throw me into it and seal it over me, and that I would be saved from the Fire tomorrow." They asked: "O so-and-so, what is the sign of that?" He said: "A Prophet will be sent from the direction of this land," and he pointed with his hand toward Makkah and Yemen. They asked: "When will we see him?" He cast his glance and saw me lying at the courtyard of my family's door, and I was the youngest of the people. He said: "If this boy lives out his life, he will see him." Not a day and night had passed before God sent His Messenger (ﷺ), and he was alive among us. We believed in him and confirmed him, but that man disbelieved in him out of rebellion and envy. We said: "O so-and-so, did you not say what you said and inform us of it?" He said: "He is not him..."'"

Ibn Ishaq said: "ʿAsim ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, ... from Qatadah, who said: 'Some of our elders narrated to me, saying: No one among the Arabs had more knowledge of the matter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) than we did. The Jews were with us, and they were people of Scripture, while we were people of idols. We had reached a point of hostility with them that they disliked. They used to say: "A Prophet who is to be sent now has drawn near in time. We will follow him, and then we will kill you with the killing of ʿAd and Iram." When God, the Mighty and Majestic, sent His Messenger (ﷺ), we followed him, and they disbelieved in him. Concerning us and them God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And previously they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved, but when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.﴾'"

Verse of poetry: "Al-Hakim and others narrated from Ibn Abi Najih, ∗∗∗ from ʿAli al-Azdi, who said: The Jews used to say:
'O God, send us this Prophet who will judge between us and the people...'"

Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated, ... from Ibn ʿAbbas: "The Jews of Khaybar used to fight Ghatafan. When they met, the Jews of Khaybar were defeated. So the Jews sought refuge in this supplication: 'O God, we ask You, by the right of Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet whom You promised to bring forth for us at the end of time, that You help us against them.' He said: 'Whenever they met, they would call upon God with this supplication, and they would defeat Ghatafan. But when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, they disbelieved in him. So God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And previously they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾, meaning, through you, O Muhammad, ﴿so the curse of God is upon the disbelievers﴾.'"

*Yastaftihun* means: they seek victory (*yastansirun*).

Al-Hakim and others mentioned that when the Banu al-Nadir were expelled from Madinah, ʿAmr ibn Saʿdi came, circled their dwellings, and saw their ruin. He reflected, then returned to the Banu Qurayzah and found them in the synagogue (*kanisah*). He blew into their horn, and they gathered. Al-Zubayr ibn Bata said: "O Abu Saʿid, where have you been since today? We have not seen you." He was someone who never left the synagogue and was devoted to Judaism. He replied: "Today I have seen signs from which we should take a lesson. I saw our brothers exiled after that might, eternity, distinguished nobility, and brilliant intellect. They left their wealth, and others took possession of it, and they went out in the manner of humiliation. By the Tawrah, this has not been imposed upon any people for whom God had any purpose. Before that, He had struck Ibn al-Ashraf in the strength of his building, in his own house, while he was secure. He struck Ibn Shaybah, their chief. He struck the Banu Qaynuqaʿ, expelled them, and they were the rabbis of the Jews, possessors of numbers, arms, and valor. He besieged them, and no one among them put out his head until he took them captive. They spoke to him about them, and he left them on condition that they leave Yathrib. O people, you have seen what you have seen. Obey me, let us come and follow Muhammad. By God, you know that he is a Prophet, and Ibn al-Hayban Abu ʿUmayr and Ibn Hawwas, who are the most knowledgeable of the Jews, told us of him and of his affair. They came from Bayt al-Maqdis, awaiting his arrival, and they ordered us to follow him and to convey their greetings to him. Then they both died upon their religion, and we buried them at our lava field." The people fell silent, and none of them spoke. He repeated these words and similar ones, and threatened them with war, captivity, and exile. Al-Zubayr ibn Bata said: "By the Tawrah, I have read his description in the Tawrah that was revealed to Musa (Moses), not in the *mathani* (repeated verses) that we have invented." Then Kaʿb ibn Usayd said to him: "What prevents you, O Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, from following him?" He said: "You." He asked: "Why?" He said: "By the Tawrah, I have never stood between you and him." Al-Zubayr said: "You are the holder of our covenant and pact. If you follow him, we will follow him, and if you refuse, we will refuse." Then ʿAmr ibn Saʿd turned to me and recounted what they had argued about, until Kaʿb said: "I have nothing in this matter except what I have said. My soul does not agree to become a follower."

This same obstacle prevented Pharaoh from following Musa, peace be upon him. When guidance became clear to him, he resolved to follow Musa. His minister Haman said to him: "You were a god worshipped, and now you will worship a lord, worshipping other than yourself?" He said: "You have spoken the truth."

Ibn Ishaq mentioned from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, who said: "I was told ... from Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, that she said: 'I was the dearest of my father's children to him and to my uncle Abu Yasir. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to Madinah, they went to him in the morning, then came back in the evening. I heard my uncle say to my father: "Is he the one?" He said: "Yes." He asked: "Do you know him and confirm him?" He said: "Yes." He asked: "What is in your soul toward him?" He said: "Enmity. By God, as long as I live..."'" 

This is an ungrateful nation, known for enmity toward the Prophets from ancient times. Their forebears and rabbis, God, glory be to Him, has told us of their harm to Musa, and He forbade us from imitating them in that. He said: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God.﴾

As for their later generations, they are the Jews who killed the Prophets. They killed Zakariyya and his son Yahya, and many Prophets. They killed seventy Prophets in a single day, then set up their market at the end of the day as if they had done nothing. They gathered to kill al-Masih and crucify him, but God protected him and honored him against being humiliated at their hands, and He cast his likeness upon another, so they killed and crucified that person. They also attempted to kill the Seal of the Prophets several times, but God protects him from them.

Whoever has this as his state, it is not strange that they chose disbelief over faith for one reason or another from the causes we have mentioned, or for two or more.

We have already mentioned that the nation of misguidance and the worshippers of the Cross agreed to revile the Lord of the worlds with the vilest abuse, and to deny things whose falsehood is known at first glance. For those feeble minds, it is not strange that they revile a human being whom God sent, deny his prophethood, and deny what clear reason indicates of his truthfulness and the validity of his message. Even if they had said about him whatever they said, it would not reach some of what they said about the Lord of the earth and the heavens, about whom they became a laughingstock among all the children of Adam.

Then a nation that agreed that the true God, glorified and exalted is He above what they say, was crucified, struck on the face, nailed, had thorns placed on His head, and was buried in the earth; then He rose on the third day, ascended, and sat upon His throne, managing the affairs of the heavens and the earth. It would not be difficult for them to agree in denying the prophethood of the one who came to revile and curse them, fight them, expose their faults, and call out their disbelief in God and His Messenger, and to bear witness to the innocence of the Messiah from them and his enmity toward them. Then he fought them, humiliated them, expelled them from their homes, and imposed the jizyah (poll tax) upon them. He informed that they are among the people of Hellfire, abiding and eternal therein, that God will not forgive them, and that they are worse than donkeys, indeed they are the worst of beasts in the sight of God.

How can one object to a nation that agreed upon the crucifixion of its worshipped god and deity, and then deliberately turned to the cross, worshipping it and venerating it, when it should have burned every cross it could burn and humiliated it to the utmost degree, since upon it they crucified their god, whom they sometimes say is God, sometimes say is His son, and sometimes say is the third of three? Thus they denied the right of their Creator and disbelieved in Him with the greatest disbelief, and reviled Him with the most vile reviling, by denying the right of His servant and Messenger and disbelieving in him.

How can it be difficult for a nation that said about the Lord of the earth and the heavens that He descended from the heaven to speak to the creation Himself, in His essence, so that they would have no proof against Him; so He wished to cut off their argument by speaking to them in His essence, so that excuses would be removed from those who neglected His covenant after He had spoken to them in His essence? So He descended in His essence from the heaven, and was joined in the womb of Mary, and took from her a veil, which is created from the aspect of the body and uncreated from the aspect of the soul. He is the one who created His body and created His mother. His mother existed before Him in the nasut (human nature), and He existed before her in the lahut (divine nature). He is the perfect God and the perfect man. And among the completeness of His mercy, blessed and exalted is He, toward His servants is that He was pleased with the shedding of His blood for them upon the wood of the cross. He enabled His enemies the Jews over His person, so that His wrath upon them would be fulfilled. They seized Him, crucified Him, struck Him on the face, spat in His face, and crowned Him with a crown of thorns upon His head. His blood sank into His finger, because if any of it had fallen to the earth, everything on its surface would have dried up, so the narcissus (nawwar) grew in the place of His crucifixion.

And since it is not within divine wisdom that God should take vengeance upon His disobedient servant who wronged Him and belittled His rank, because the station of the Lord is exalted and the station of the servant has fallen, He, glorified is He, wished to take retribution from the human being who is a god like Him. So He took retribution for Adam's sin by the crucifixion of Jesus the Messiah, who is a god equal to Him in divinity. Thus the Son of God, who is God, was crucified at the ninth hour of Friday. These are their own words in their books.

So how can a nation that agreed upon this regarding its worshipped deity find it difficult to say about His servant and Messenger that he is a sorcerer, a liar, an empowered king, and the like?

For this reason some of the kings of India said: As for the Christians, if their enemies among the people of the religions fight them by the Law, I see their fighting by reason. Although we do not approve of fighting anyone, I make an exception of these people from the entire world, because they intended to oppose reason, held enmity against it, and deviated from all the clear legal and rational interests of the world. They believed every impossibility to be possible, and built from this a law that does not lead to the welfare of any kind of created being, but rather makes the intelligent person who follows it foolish, the rightly guided person a fool, the good ugly, and the ugly good. For whoever has at the root of his creed, in which he was raised, the offense against the Creator, the disparagement of Him, the reviling of Him with the most vile reviling, and the description of Him with what changes His beautiful attributes, is more fitting that he would begin offense against a creature, and describe him with what changes his beautiful attributes.

And if the struggle against these people were required only because of the generality of their harms, which cannot be counted in their aspects, just as it is required to kill an animal harmful by its nature, they would be deserving of it.

The point is that those who chose this doctrine about the Lord of the worlds, while glorifying Him, declaring Him free of imperfection, exalting Him, and describing Him with what is fitting for Him, are those who chose disbelief in His servant and Messenger and denied his prophethood. And those who chose the worship of images that they drew with their own hands on the walls, decorated in red, yellow, and blue, which if dogs approached them they would urinate upon them, to which they gave the utmost submission, humiliation, reverence, and weeping, and asked of them forgiveness, mercy, provision, and victory: these are the ones who chose the denial of the Seal of the Messengers over believing in him, affirming him, and following him.

And those who declared their metropolitans and patriarchs free of having a consort, a son, and the like, for the One, the Eternal Refuge, are those who denied the prophethood of His servant and the Seal of His Messengers. And those who chose a prayer in which the most devout and ascetic of them stands, urinating on his shin and thighs, then faces the east and then prostrates upon his face, worshipping the crucified god, and opens the prayer by saying: "Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name; thy kingdom come; thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread."

Then he speaks to the one beside him, and perhaps asks him about the price of wine and pork, what he earned in gambling, and what he cooked in his house. Perhaps he breaks wind while in his prayer, and if he wished he would urinate in his place if he could, then he calls upon that image which is the product of human hands.

So those who chose this prayer over the prayer of one who, when he stands for his prayer, purifies his limbs, his garments, and his body from impurity, faces the Sacred House, glorifies God, praises Him, declares Him free of imperfection, and extols Him with what He deserves, then speaks to Him with His words containing the best praise of Him, His glorification, His exaltation, His unity, the singling out of Him in worship and in seeking help, and asks of Him the most exalted request, which is guidance to the path of His pleasure, which He specified for those whom He has blessed, apart from the path of the two nations: those who earned His anger, who are the Jews, and those who went astray, who are the Christians. Then he gives every limb its share of humility, submission, and servitude, together with the utmost praise and extolling of God, Lord of the worlds. He does not turn away from his worshipped Lord with his face or his heart, and does not speak a word to anyone. Rather he has emptied his heart for his worshipped Lord, and turned toward Him with his heart and face. He does not break wind in his prayer, and does not place between his eyes a manufactured image that he calls upon and humbly beseeches. Those who chose that image, which in reality is a mockery of the one worshipped, which the created being would not accept for himself, let alone that the Creator would accept it, in this prayer, which if presented to one who has even a little measure of intellect, the disparity between the two would become apparent to him. These are the ones who chose the denial of the Seal of the Messengers, Muhammad, His Messenger and servant, over believing in him, affirming him, and following him.

The intelligent person, when he weighs what they chose and desired against what they turned away from, will see clearly that these people chose misguidance over guidance, error over right direction, the ugly over the good, and falsehood over truth. They chose from doctrines the most false, and from deeds the most ugly. Their bishops, patriarchs, and monks agreed upon this, let alone their common people.

(Section)

None of the Muslims has said that all those you mentioned, young and old, male and female, free and slave, monk and priest, have had guidance made clear to them. Rather, most of them are ignorant, like grazing beasts, turning away from seeking guidance, let alone having it made clear to them. They are imitators of their chiefs, their great ones, and their scholars. These are the very few, and they are the ones who chose disbelief over belief after guidance had been made clear.

And what difficulty arises for the intellect in this? There have always been people who choose it out of envy while knowing its falsehood out of arrogance; the falsehood among them is chosen out of ignorance and imitation of one whom they think well of; among them are those who choose it out of envy and rebellion; among them are those who choose it out of greed and desire for food, or rank and leadership; among them are those who choose it out of love for a form and infatuation; among them are those who choose it out of fear; among them are those who choose it out of haughtiness; and among them are those who choose it for ease and comfort. Thus the causes of choosing disbelief are not confined to love of leadership and eating.

The one who is due the punishment is the one who does not prostrate to Him, the Glorified, and He humiliated him by abandoning prostration to Him. He informed that there is no one to honor him, and he has been humiliated before his Lord because he did not prostrate to Him.

(A subtle point)

Here, many people are singled out for prostration, whereas in Surat al-Nahl it is general, in His words: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels﴾ [al-Nahl: 49]. This is the prostration of humbling, subjugation and submission (sujud al-dhull wa'l-qahr wa'l-khudu'). Every single being is subject to His lordship, humbled before His might, and subdued under His sovereignty, exalted is He.

(A benefit)

Disobedience is a cause of the servant's humiliation before his Lord and his falling from His regard.

Al-Hasan al-Basri (d. 110 AH) said: "They were humiliated before Him, so they disobeyed Him. Had they been honored before Him, He would have protected them." When the servant is humiliated before Allah, no one honors him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whomever Allah humiliates, there is none to honor him﴾.

And if people glorify them outwardly, out of their need for them or out of fear of their evil, yet in their hearts they regard them as the most contemptible and worthless of things.

[Section: Sins weaken the glorification of the Lord in the heart]

Among the punishments of sins is that they weaken in the heart the glorification of the Lord, the Majestic in His majesty, and inevitably weaken His gravity in the servant's heart, whether he wills it or refuses. Had the gravity and greatness of Allah been firmly established in the servant's heart, he would not have dared to commit His acts of disobedience. Sometimes the deluded one is deceived and says: "What drives me to acts of disobedience is my good expectation (husn al-raja') and my hope for His pardon, not a weakness in my heart's sense of His greatness." This is one of the self's deceptions, for the greatness and majesty of Allah in the servant's heart necessitate glorifying His sacred prohibitions, and glorifying His sacred prohibitions prevents him from sins. Those who are bold against His acts of disobedience have not measured Allah with His due measure. How can one who finds His command and prohibition insignificant measure Him with His due measure, or glorify and magnify Him, or hope for His gravity and revere Him? This is one of the most impossible impossibilities and clearest falsehoods. It is punishment enough for the disobedient that the glorification of Allah, the Majestic in His majesty, and the glorification of His sacred prohibitions wither away from his heart, and His right becomes insignificant to him.

Part of the punishment for this is that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, removes His awe from the hearts of creation, so they become contemptuous of him and treat him lightly, just as His command became insignificant to him and he treated it lightly. In proportion to the servant's love for Allah, people love him; in proportion to his fear of Allah, creation fears him; and in proportion to his glorification of Allah and His sacred prohibitions, people glorify him. How can a servant violate the sacred prohibitions of Allah and hope that people will not violate his sacred prohibitions? Or how can Allah's right be insignificant to him while Allah does not make it insignificant to people? Or how can he treat the disobedience of Allah lightly while creation does not treat him lightly? He, glorified be He, has indicated this in His Book when mentioning the punishments of sins, and that He made its perpetrators fall back (arkasa) because of what they earned, covered over their hearts, sealed them by their sins, forgot them as they forgot Him, humiliated them as they humiliated His religion, and neglected them as they neglected His command. For this reason, He, the Exalted, said in the verse about the prostration of created things to Him: ﴿And whomever Allah humiliates, there is none to honor him﴾.

Since prostration to Him seemed insignificant to them, and they treated it lightly and did not perform it, Allah humiliated them, and so there was no one to honor them after Allah humiliated them. And who honors one whom Allah has humiliated? Or who humiliates one whom Allah has honored?

[Section: Sins cause the loss of honor]

Among their punishments is the loss of standing, rank and honor before Allah and before His creation. The most honored of creatures before Allah is the most pious among them, and the closest of them to Him in rank is the most obedient to Him. In proportion to the servant's obedience, he holds his rank before Him. When he disobeys Him and opposes His command, he falls from His regard, and so He drops him from the hearts of His servants. When he no longer has standing with creation, and they treat him lightly, they deal with him according to that. So he lives among them in the worst of lives: obscure in repute, fallen in status, wretched in condition, with no esteem, no joy and no happiness. The obscurity of repute, the fall of rank and standing bring with them every grief, anxiety and sorrow, with no happiness or joy. And where is this pain from the pleasure of disobedience, were it not for the intoxication of desire?

Among the greatest blessings of Allah upon the servant is that He raises his mention among the worlds and exalts his rank. For this reason, He singled out His prophets and messengers with what He did not give to others, as the Exalted said: ﴿And mention Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and vision. Indeed, We purified them with a pure quality: remembrance of the abode﴾ [Sad: 45-46].

That is: We granted them a distinction, namely the good remembrance by which they are remembered in this abode, which is the "tongue of truth" (lisan al-sidq) that Abraham the Friend, upon him be peace, asked for when he said: ﴿And make for me a tongue of truth among the later generations﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 84].

And He, glorified and exalted, said about him and his descendants: ﴿And We gave them of Our mercy and made for them a tongue of truth, elevated﴾ [Maryam: 50].

And He said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And We raised for you your mention﴾ [al-Sharh: 4].

So the followers of the messengers have a share of this in accordance with their inheritance of their obedience and following of them, and whoever opposes them is far from this in accordance with his opposition and disobedience to them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 22, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And their clothing therein is silk.﴾

Here there is an issue, and this is the place to mention it. Allah, glorified and exalted, has informed that the clothing of the people of Paradise is silk. And it is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said:

"Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter."

It is agreed upon as authentic, from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab and Anas ibn Malik.

There has been disagreement about the intended meaning of this hadith. A group among the early (salaf) and later (khalaf) scholars said: he will not wear silk in Paradise, but he will wear other garments.

They said: as for His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And their clothing therein is silk﴾, it falls under the general (ʿam) that has been specified (makhsus).

But the majority (al-Jumhur) said: this is from the threats (al-waʿid) which have the same ruling as similar threat-texts indicating that the act necessitates this ruling, though it may be withheld from taking effect by an impediment.

The text and the consensus (ijmaʿ) establish that repentance prevents the threat from taking effect. Also preventing it from taking effect are the erasing good deeds, the expiating calamities, the supplication of Muslims, the intercession of whomever Allah permits to intercede for him, and the intercession of the Most Merciful of the merciful toward Himself. Thus this hadith is similar to the other hadith: "Whoever drinks wine in this world will not drink it in the Hereafter." And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And He will reward them for what they endured with a garden and silk﴾, and He said: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade﴾.

(Benefit)

They differed concerning the genitive (jarr) and accusative (naṣb) of ﴿lu'lu'﴾ (pearls). Whoever reads it in the accusative has two options:

The first: it is in coordination (ʿaṭf) with the place (mawḍiʿ) of His saying: ﴿of bracelets﴾ (min asāwira).

The second: it is accusative by a verb omitted, indicated by the first, meaning: "and they will be adorned with pearls." Whoever reads it in the genitive, it is coordinated with "gold" (dhahab), and then it allows two meanings:

The first: they will have bracelets of gold and bracelets of pearls. The second: the bracelets may be composed of both together, gold set with pearls. And Allah knows best what He intended.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn Rizq related to me, Zayd ibn al-Habbab related to us, who said: Utba ibn Saʿd, judge of al-Rayy, related to me, from Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Shamr ibn ʿAtiyya, from Kaʿb, who said:

"Indeed, Allah, mighty and majestic, has an angel since the day He created (the world) who fashions the ornaments of the people of Paradise until the Hour arises. If a single piece of the ornaments of the people of Paradise were brought out, it would outshine the sunlight. So do not ask, after this, about the ornaments of the people of Paradise."

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya ibn Kathir al-ʿAnbari related to us, from my father, from Ashʿath, from al-Hasan, who said:

"Ornaments in Paradise are more beautiful on men than on women."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 22, verse 25:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation [from the right course] through wrongdoing - We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾. The verb "irada" (to intend) is not transitive with the preposition "bi" (in/with), but it has been construed here to carry the meaning of "yahumma fihi bi-kadhā" (he resolves upon something therein).

And this is more emphatic than mere intention.

So the mention of "bi" here points to the deserving of punishment at the moment of intention, even if it is not a firm resolve.

(Benefit)

Among its distinctive features is that one is punished therein for the resolve to commit evil deeds, even if one does not actually do them. He, Exalted, says: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation [from the right course] through wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment﴾.

So reflect on how the verb "irada" is here followed by "bi". One does not say "aradtu bi-kadhā" (I intended with such-and-such) except when it is construed to carry the meaning of the verb "hamma" (to resolve), for one says "hamamtu bi-kadhā" (I resolved upon such-and-such). Thus He threatens whoever resolves to commit wrongdoing therein with making him taste the painful punishment.

From this is the multiplication of the degrees (magnitudes) of evil deeds therein, not their quantities. For the evil deed's recompense is an evil deed, but a great evil deed's recompense is its like, and a small one's recompense is its like. Yet an evil deed within the Sacred Precinct of God, His city, and upon His carpet, is more binding and greater than it at the edge of the lands. For this reason, one who disobeys the King upon the carpet of his kingdom is not like one who disobeys him in a remote place of his house and carpet. This is the decisive resolution of the dispute concerning the multiplication of evil deeds, and God knows best.

[Chapter: The division of Makkah is prohibited, because it is the abode of rites]

As for Makkah, there is in it another matter that prevents its division, even if the division of the other towns were obligatory. It is that it cannot be owned, for it is the abode of rites (nusuk), the place of worship of creation, and the Sacred Precinct of the Lord, Exalted is He, which He made for mankind equally, for the one who dwells there and the one who comes from outside. It is therefore an endowment (waqf) from God for the worlds, and they are equal therein. "And Mina is the resting place of whoever arrives first." God, Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar from the way of God and the Sacred Mosque, which We made for the people equally, the resident therein and the visitor, and whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing - We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [al-Hajj: 25]. Here "al-Masjid al-Haram" (the Sacred Mosque) means the entire Sacred Precinct, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs﴾ [al-Tawbah: 28], which refers to the whole Sacred Precinct. And in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Exalted is He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa﴾ [al-Isra: 1]. And in the Sahih: that he (ﷺ) "was taken by night from the house of Umm Hani'".

God, Exalted, says: ﴿That is for one whose family is not present at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [al-Baqarah: 196]. It is agreed that what is meant is not the presence at the very place of prayer, but rather presence within the Sacred Precinct and nearness to it. The context of the verse of Hajj indicates this, for He said: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation through wrongdoing - We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [al-Hajj: 25].

This is certainly not restricted to the station of prayer; rather, what is meant is the entire Sacred Precinct. He who made it equal for the people, the resident therein and the visitor, is the One who threatened whoever bars from it and whoever intends to deviate through wrongdoing therein. The Sacred Precinct and its sacred sites, such as as-Safa and al-Marwah, al-Mas'a, Mina, Arafat, and Muzdalifah, are not exclusive to anyone over anyone; rather they are shared among people, since they are the place of their rites and worship. They are a mosque from God, endowed and placed by Him for His creation. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) refused that a building be erected for him at Mina to shade him from the heat, and he said: "Mina is the resting place of whoever arrives first."

For this reason, the majority of the imams of the early and later generations held that it is not permissible to sell the lands of Makkah or to rent its houses. This is the position of Mujahid and 'Ata' regarding the people of Makkah, of Malik regarding the people of Madinah, of Abu Hanifah regarding the people of Iraq, of Sufyan al-Thawri, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh.

Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, narrated from 'Alqamah ibn Nadlah, who said: "The houses (ribā') of Makkah were called as-sawa'ib (the free) in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), Abu Bakr and 'Umar. Whoever was in need would dwell, and whoever was wealthy would let others dwell."

It is also narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar: "Whoever consumes the rents of the houses of Makkah, he is only consuming the Fire of Hell in his belly." Al-Daraqutni narrated it as marfu' to the Prophet (ﷺ), and in it: "Indeed God has made Makkah sacred, so the sale of its houses and the consumption of their price is forbidden."

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'ammar narrated to us, from Layth, from 'Ata', Tawus and Mujahid, that they said: It is disliked to sell the houses (ribā') of Makkah or to rent out its dwellings.

Imam Ahmad mentioned from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: "Whoever eats from the rent of the houses of Makkah, he is only eating Fire in his belly."

Ahmad also said: Hushaym narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Mujahid, "from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: It was forbidden to rent the houses of Makkah and to sell its houses (ribā')."

And he mentioned from 'Ata', who said: It was forbidden to rent the houses of Makkah.

Ahmad also said: Ishaq ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote to the governor of the people of Makkah forbidding him from renting the houses of Makkah, and said that it is unlawful.

Ahmad related from 'Umar that he forbade the people of Makkah from making doors for their houses, so that the visitor might lodge wherever he wished; and he related from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, that he forbade closing the doors of the houses of Makkah: he forbade one who has no door for his house from making one for it, and one who has a door from closing it. This was during the days of the season (pilgrimage).

Those who permit sale and rent said: The evidence for the permissibility of this is the Book of God, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the practice of his Companions and rightly-guided caliphs.

God, Exalted, says: ﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth﴾ [al-Hashr: 8], and He said: ﴿Those who emigrated and were expelled from their homes﴾ [Al 'Imran: 195], and He said: ﴿God only forbids you from those who fought you over religion and expelled you from your homes﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 9]. Thus He attributed the homes to them, and this is an attribution of ownership. And the Prophet (ﷺ), when he was asked: "Where will you descend tomorrow in your house in Makkah?", said: "Did 'Aqil leave us any houses (ribā')?" He did not say, "I have no house," but rather he confirmed their attribution and informed that 'Aqil had seized them, and did not remove them from his hand. The attribution of their homes to them in the hadiths is too numerous to mention, such as the house of Umm Hani', the house of Khadijah, the house of Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh, and others. They used to inherit them just as they inherited movable property. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did 'Aqil leave us any dwelling?"

'Aqil had inherited the houses of Abu Talib, for he was a disbeliever, and 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, did not inherit from him because of the difference of religion between them, so 'Aqil seized the houses.

And they never ceased, before the Hijrah and after it, indeed before the mission and after it, that whoever died, his house passed to his heirs, up to now. Safwan ibn Umayyah sold a house to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, for four thousand dirhams, and he made it a prison. If sale and inheritance are permissible, then rent is even more permissible. This is the stance of both parties, as you see, and their arguments in strength and clarity cannot be repelled; the proofs of God and His clear evidences do not cancel one another, but rather confirm one another, and it is obligatory to act upon all of their implications. The duty is to follow the truth wherever it is.

The correct position, then, is to hold according to the implications of the evidences from both sides: that houses can be owned, gifted, inherited and sold, and that the transfer of ownership applies to the building, not to the land and the open ground. So if its building is destroyed, he has no right to sell the land; rather he may rebuild it and restore it as it was, and he has the greater right to it, to dwell in it and to let whomever he wishes dwell in it. But he has no right to exchange for the benefit of dwelling by a contract of rent, for this benefit is only one that he deserves to be given priority in and to be specially entitled to because of his precedence and need. When he becomes free of need for it, he has no right to exchange it, like sitting in open courtyards and wide roads, residing at mines and other shared benefits and properties, whoever precedes to them has the greater right to them as long as he benefits from them; when he ceases to need them, he has no right to exchange them.
