Whatever heart absorbs them, a black spot is marked on it, and whatever heart rejects them, a white spot is marked on it, until hearts become of two kinds: a black heart, dark and inverted like a cup, that recognizes no good and rejects no evil except what has been absorbed from its desire; and a white heart, which no trial harms as long as the heavens and the earth endure."

He likened the presenting of trials to hearts, bit by bit, to the presenting of the reeds of a mat, which are its strands, bit by bit. He divided the hearts, when the trials are presented to them, into two categories:

A heart that is presented with a trial absorbs it, just as a sponge absorbs water, and a black spot is marked on it. It keeps absorbing every trial presented to it until it turns black and becomes inverted. This is the meaning of His words, "like a cup turned upside down" (﴿كالكوز مجخيا﴾), meaning overturned and inverted. When it has blackened and become inverted, two dangerous diseases afflict it, and both lead it to destruction. The first is that the good becomes confused for it with the evil, so it recognizes no good and denounces no evil. This disease may become so entrenched that it considers the good to be evil and the evil to be good, the sunnah (the prophetic way) to be bid'ah (innovation) and the bid'ah to be sunnah, the truth to be falsehood and the falsehood to be truth. The second is that it makes its desire the judge over what the Messenger (ﷺ) brought, and it submits to and follows its desire.

A white heart, in which the light of faith has shone and its lamp has blossomed, rejects and repels any trial presented to it, and its light, radiance and strength increase.

The trials that are presented to hearts are the causes of their sickness. They are trials of desires and trials of doubts, trials of error and misguidance, trials of sins and innovations, and trials of injustice and ignorance. The first kind causes the corruption of intention and will, and the second causes the corruption of knowledge and belief.

The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, divided hearts into four, as authentically related from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman:
"The hearts are four: a heart that is bare, in which there is a shining lamp, and that is the heart of the believer. A heart that is covered, and that is the heart of the disbeliever. A heart that is inverted, and that is the heart of the hypocrite, who recognizes and then denies, sees and then becomes blind. And a heart that is fed by two streams, the stream of faith and the stream of hypocrisy, and it belongs to whichever of the two prevails over it."

As for his words, "a bare heart," it means one stripped of everything other than Allah and His Messenger. It has been stripped and kept free of everything other than the truth.

"In which there is a shining lamp" refers to the lamp of faith. By its being bare, he indicates its safety from the doubts of falsehood and the desires of error, and by the presence of the lamp in it, he indicates its illumination and brightness with the light of knowledge and faith.

By the covered heart, he refers to the heart of the disbeliever, because it is enclosed within its covering and veil, so the light of knowledge and faith does not reach it, as Allah, the Exalted, said, relating the words of the Jews:
﴿And they say, "Our hearts are covered."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 88]
It is the plural of aghlaf, meaning one enclosed in its covering, like qalaf and aqlaf. This veil is the enclosures (akinnah) that Allah has placed over their hearts as a punishment for them for rejecting the truth and being arrogant toward accepting it. They are enclosures over the hearts, deafness in the ears, and blindness in the eyes. It is the hidden barrier spoken of in His words, the Exalted:
﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier, and We place over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness.﴾ [al-Isra': 45-46]
So when the purity of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah) and the purity of following (mutaba'ah, following the Prophet) are mentioned to these hearts, their owners turn their backs in aversion.

By the inverted heart, which is the overturned one, he refers to the heart of the hypocrite, as Allah, the Exalted, said:
﴿Why have you become two groups concerning the hypocrites, while Allah has overturned them for what they earned?﴾ [al-Nisa': 88]
That is, He inverted them and returned them to the falsehood they were in, because of their earning and their false deeds. This is the worst and most wicked of hearts, for it believes falsehood to be truth and allies itself with its adherents, and it considers truth to be falsehood and opposes its people. So Allah is the One sought for help.

By the heart that has two streams, he refers to the heart in which faith has not taken firm root and whose lamp has not blossomed, since it has not been purified for the pure truth with which Allah sent His Messenger. Rather, it contains a portion of that truth and a portion of its opposite. At times it is closer to disbelief than to faith, and at other times closer to faith than to disbelief. The judgment belongs to what prevails, and it is to that that it returns.

**[Section]**

As for His words, ﴿that He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease, and the hard-hearted﴾, the particle here retains its original sense: it is the *lam* of wisdom and causation (*lam al-hikmah wa'l-ta'lil*). God, glorified is He, informs us that He made what Satan had cast into the wish of the Messenger a test and a trial for His servants. Two groups were thereby put to trial: those in whose hearts is a disease, and those whose hearts are hard. He also made the believers know that the Qur'an and the Messenger are true, and that Satan's casting is false. So they believed in this, and their hearts became humbly submissive to it. This is a sought-after and intended end through this divine decree and measure.

God, glorified is He, made hearts into three categories: diseased, hard, and humbly submissive (*mukhbitah*). This is because a heart is either dry and rigid, not softening to the truth in acknowledgment and submission, or it is not like that. The first is the state of hard, stony hearts that do not accept what is instilled in them, in which the truth is not impressed and beneficial knowledge is not engraved, and which do not soften to the performance of righteous deeds. As for the second type, it is either that the truth is firmly established in it and does not depart from it, because of its strength together with its softness, or that it is established with weakness and dissolution. The second is the diseased heart, and the first is the sound, humbly submissive heart. It combines firmness, purity, and softness: it sees the truth through its purity, is strengthened in it through its firmness, and shows mercy to creatures through its softness. As in a transmitted report: "The hearts are the vessels of God on His earth, so the most beloved of them to God are the firmest, the softest and the purest."

As God, the Exalted, said of the people of these hearts: ﴿Hard against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ (48:29).

This is a description by Him of the believers who recognized faith through the purity of their hearts, were firm against the disbelievers through their hardness, and showed mercy among themselves through their softness. This is because the heart is one of the organs of the body. It is the noblest of its organs and its obeyed sovereign. Every organ, such as the hand for instance, is either rigid and dry, not bending and not gripping, or it grips weakly, and this is like the hard heart. Or it is diseased, weak, and incapable, and due to its weakness and disease, this is like the one who has a disease. Or it is gripping with strength and softness, and this is like the knowing, merciful heart. Through knowledge it has come out of the disease arising from desire and doubt, and through mercy it has come out of hardness. For this reason God, glorified is He, described those other than the owners of the diseased and hard hearts by knowledge, faith, and humble submission. So reflect on the manifestation of His wisdom, glorified is He, in the owners of these hearts, who are the whole community. He informed us that those given knowledge know that it is the truth from their Lord, just as He informed us that they say, regarding the ambiguous (*mutashabih*) verses, "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord." Both attributes are subject to doubt. So their portion of it was faith, and the portion of the owners of hearts deviating from soundness was trial. For this reason God, glorified is He, made the firm (*ihkam*) rulings of His verses correspond to what Satan casts. The firm verses correspond to the ambiguous ones. So the making firm here is like the sending down of the firm verses there, and the abrogation (*naskh*) of what Satan casts here corresponds to the referral of the ambiguous to the firm there. Abrogation here means lifting what Satan cast, not lifting what the Lord, glorified is He, legislated. Abrogation has another meaning as well: abrogating from the understanding of the addressees what they understood from it that was not intended, and that the wording did not indicate, even if it gave that impression. Just as the Companions applied the term "abrogation" to His words: ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, God will call you to account for it, then He forgives whom He wills﴾ (2:284). They said: "It was abrogated by His words: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾ (2:286), and the rest of the verse."

This is abrogation of understanding, not abrogation of an established ruling, since being called to account does not necessarily entail punishment, either in the Hereafter or in this world. For this reason He made the call to account general to them all, then afterwards informed that He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. So understanding from the verse the taking to task, which is punishment, is loading it beyond its capacity. Therefore this meaning was lifted from their understanding by His words: ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾, to the end of it.

This is the lifting of an understanding of something other than the intended meaning of what the angel cast, and that is the lifting of what someone other than the angel cast into their hearing or into the wish. Abrogation has a third meaning according to the Companions and the Successors (*tabi'un*): leaving the apparent meaning, either by specifying a general ruling or by restricting an absolute one. This is very frequent in their speech. It has a fourth meaning, which later scholars know and on which they have agreed: lifting a ruling entirely after its establishment by a lifting proof. So these are four meanings of abrogation, and making firm has three meanings.

The first is making firm that corresponds to the ambiguous, as in His words: ﴿He it is who sent down to you the Book, in it are firm verses, which are the mother of the Book, and others ambiguous﴾ (3:7).

The second is making firm that corresponds to the abrogation of what Satan casts, as in His words: ﴿Then God abrogates what Satan casts, then God makes His verses firm﴾ (22:52). This making firm encompasses all His verses: it is their establishment, confirmation, and clarification. Among its uses is His words: ﴿A Book whose verses are made firm﴾ (11:1).

The third is making firm that corresponds to the abrogated verses, as the early generations often say: "This verse is firm and not abrogated." This is because making firm sometimes occurs in the revelation, and then it corresponds to what Satan casts in his wish, whether what the transmitter casts or what enters the transmitter's hearing. The ruling here is what God sent down. God made it firm, that is, He distinguished it from its confusion with what was not sent down, and He separated from it what is not from it by invalidating it. Sometimes it occurs in preserving the revealed text and its continuance, so it is not abrogated after its establishment. And sometimes it occurs in the meaning of the revealed text and its interpretation, which is distinguishing the intended meaning from other meanings so that it is not confused with them.

The point is that His words ﴿so that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ have the *lam* of causation in its original sense. This test and trial manifest the three different hearts. The hard and diseased hearts have had their concealed doubt and disbelief exposed. The humbly submissive heart has had its concealed faith and guidance exposed, along with increased love for it and increased hatred of disbelief and polytheism and aversion from them. This is among the greatest wisdoms of this casting.

**[Section: The difference between the angel's inspiration and Satan's casting]**

The difference between the inspiration of the angel and the casting of Satan is in several respects:

Among them: whatever is pleasing to God and in accordance with what His Messenger brought is from the angel, and whatever is for other than Him and not pleasing to Him is from Satan's casting.

Among them: whatever produces turning to God, repentance to Him, remembrance of Him, and an ascending aspiration toward Him is from the angel's casting, and whatever produces the opposite is from Satan's casting.

Among them: whatever produces intimacy, light in the heart, and expansion of the chest is from the angel, and whatever produces the opposite is from Satan.

Among them: whatever produces tranquility and calm is from the angel, and whatever produces anxiety, agitation, and turmoil is from Satan.

The angelic inspiration is frequent in pure, clean hearts that have been illuminated by God's light. The angel has a connection with them and an affinity between him and them, for he is good and pure and only approaches a heart that suits him. So the angel's whisper into this heart is more frequent than Satan's whisper. As for a dark heart that has blackened with the smoke of desires and doubts, Satan's casting and whispering into it are more frequent than the angel's whisper.

**[Section: On the division of hearts into sound, sick, and dead]**

Since the heart is described as living or its opposite, it is divided according to this into these three states.

The sound heart is the sound (*salim*) heart, which none will be saved on the Day of Resurrection except one who comes to God with it, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿The Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to God with a sound heart﴾ (26:88–89).

The word *salim* is "sound," and it follows this pattern because it denotes attributes, like *tawil* (long), *qasir* (short), and *zarif* (witty). So the sound heart is one in which soundness has become a stable attribute, like *alim* (knowing) and *qadir* (capable). Also, it is the opposite of the diseased, the sick, and the ailing.

People's expressions differ regarding the meaning of the sound heart. The comprehensive matter about it is that it is the one that has been freed from every desire that contradicts God's command and prohibition, and from every doubt that opposes His report. It is free from servitude to anything other than Him, and free from judging by other than His Messenger. It is free in loving anything alongside God, and from fearing, hoping in, relying upon, turning to, humbling itself to, and preferring the pleasure of others over His pleasure in every circumstance, and it keeps far from His wrath by every means. This is the reality of servitude that is only fit for God alone.

So the sound heart is the one free from any polytheism toward other than God in any way. Rather, its servitude is purely for God, the Exalted: in intention, love, reliance, turning, humble submission, fear, and hope. Its deeds are purely for God. If it loves, it loves for God's sake; if it hates, it hates for God's sake; if it gives, it gives for God; if it withholds, it withholds for God. And this is not sufficient for it until it is free from submission and judging by anyone other than the Messenger of God (ﷺ). It firmly ties its heart to him, in following and imitating him alone, above anyone else, in statements and deeds. These are the statements of the heart, which are beliefs; and the statements of the tongue, which are reports of what is in the heart; and the deeds of the heart, which are intention, love, dislike, and their consequences; and the deeds of the limbs.

The judge over all of this, in its smallest and greatest matters, is what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought. It does not advance ahead of him with any belief, statement, or deed, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger﴾ (49:1).

That is, do not speak until he speaks, and do not act until he commands. One of the early generations said: "No act, however small, is without two registers being opened for it: why? and how?" That is, why did you do it, and how did you do it? The first is a question about the cause of the act, its motive, and its driver: is it an immediate personal benefit of the doer, a worldly aim such as love of praise from people or fear of their blame, or attracting something desired immediately, or repelling something disliked immediately? Or is the motive of the act fulfilling the rights of servitude and seeking closeness and affection toward the Lord, glorified is He, and seeking a means to Him?

The place of this question is: were you obliged to do this act for your Master, or did you do it for your own desire and whim?

The second is a question about following the Messenger, peace be upon him, in that worship: was that deed something I legislated for you through my Messenger, or was it a deed I did not legislate and did not approve?

The first is a question about sincerity, and the second about following. God, glorified is He, accepts no deed except with both.

The way to be freed from the first question is by purifying sincerity, and the way to be freed from the second question is by achieving following. The sound heart is free from an intention that contradicts sincerity, and from a desire that contradicts following. This is the reality of the sound heart, to which salvation and happiness are guaranteed.

**[Section on the dead heart]**

The second heart is the opposite of this: the dead heart, with no life in it. It does not know its Lord, and does not worship Him by His command or by what He loves and approves. Rather, it stands with its desires and pleasures, even if there is in them the wrath and anger of its Lord. It does not care, when it wins its desire and portion, whether its Lord is pleased or angered. It is a servant of other than God: in love, fear, hope, pleasure, anger, glorification, and humiliation. If it loves, it loves for its desire; if it hates, it hates for its desire; if it gives, it gives for its desire; if it withholds, it withholds for its desire. Its desire is more preferred by it and more beloved to it than the pleasure of its Master. Desire is its leader, passion its guide, ignorance its driver, and heedlessness its mount. It is immersed in thinking about achieving its worldly aims, and intoxicated with the drunkenness of desire and love of the fleeting. It is called to God and to the Hereafter from a far place, so it does not respond to the adviser, and follows every rebellious devil. The world angers it and pleases it. Desire deafens and blinds it to everything except falsehood. In this world it is like what was said about Layla:

*An enemy to whoever opposes her, and at peace with her people,*
*and whoever Layla brings near, he loves and draws closest.*

So associating with the owner of this heart is sickness, his companionship is poison, and sitting with him is destruction.

**[Section on the diseased heart]**

The third heart is a heart that has life, but with a defect in it. It has two sources of nourishment, one of which supplies it at one time and the other at another time, depending on which prevails over it. In it is what is the source of its life: love of God, faith in Him, sincerity toward Him, and reliance upon Him. And in it is what is the source of its ruin and destruction: love of desires, preference for them, eagerness to obtain them, envy, pride, self-admiration, love of exaltation, and corruption on earth through leadership. It is tested between two callers: one calls it to God, His Messenger, and the Last Day; the other calls it to the fleeting world. It only answers whichever of them is nearer its gate and closer to its neighborhood.

So the first heart is living, humbly submissive, soft, and aware. The second is dry and dead. The third is diseased. It is either closer to safety or closer to destruction.

God, glorified is He, has gathered these three hearts in His words:

﴿We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he desired, Satan cast into his desire. Then God abrogates what Satan casts, then God makes His verses firm, and God is Knowing, Wise.﴾ (22:52)

﴿So that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and the hard-hearted, and the wrongdoers are in extreme schism.﴾ (22:53)

﴿And that those given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it and their hearts become humbly submissive to it. Indeed God guides those who believe to a straight path.﴾ (22:54)

In these verses God, glorified and exalted is He, made the hearts three: two tested hearts and one saved heart. The two tested ones are the heart in which there is disease and the hard heart. The saved one is the believing heart humbly submissive to its Lord. It is the one at peace with Him, submissive to Him, yielding and obedient.

That is because the heart and the other organs are meant to be sound, without any defect, able to perform what they were made for and created for. Their deviation from uprightness is either through dryness and hardness, and the inability to do what is required of them, like a paralyzed hand, a mute tongue, a flat nose, a man without sexual capacity, or an eye that sees nothing. Or it is through a disease or defect in them that prevents them from perfectly performing these acts and doing them correctly. For this reason the hearts were divided into these three categories.

The sound, healthy heart has nothing between it and accepting the truth, loving it, and preferring it except its perception. It perceives the truth correctly and fully submits to it and accepts it.

The dead, hard heart does not accept it and does not submit to it.

The diseased heart: if its disease prevails over it, it joins the dead, hard heart; and if its soundness prevails over it, it joins the sound heart.

So what Satan casts into the ears as words, and into the hearts as doubts and suspicions, is a trial for these two hearts, and a strength for the living, sound heart. This is because it rejects that, dislikes it, and hates it, knowing that the truth is in its opposite. So its heart humbly submits to the truth, is at peace, and yields. It knows the falsehood of what Satan cast, so its faith in the truth and its love for it increase, and its disbelief in falsehood and its aversion to it increase. So the tested heart is always in doubt about Satan's casting. As for the sound, healthy heart, what Satan casts never harms it at all.

Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

By the covered heart, he refers to the heart of the disbeliever, because it is enclosed within its covering and veil, so the light of knowledge and faith does not reach it, as Allah, the Exalted, said, relating the words of the Jews:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 22, verse 70:

Allah, glory be to Him, knew before He brought His servants into existence their conditions, what they would do, and where they would end up. Then He brought them out into this abode so that what He knew about them would become manifest, just as He knew it. He tested them with command and prohibition, good and evil, by means of what He made manifest of what He knew. Thus they deserved praise and blame, reward and punishment, on account of the actions and attributes that subsisted in them, which corresponded to the prior knowledge, and they did not deserve that while those things were in His knowledge before they performed them. So He sent His messengers, revealed His books and prescribed His laws as an excuse to them (i'dhar) and as the establishment of proof against them (iqamat al-hujjah), lest they say: "Why do You punish us for Your knowledge of us? This does not fall under our acquisition (kasb) and our power." So when His knowledge of them became manifest through their actions, the punishment was incurred upon what He knew, which the trial and the testing made manifest. Just as He tested them with His command and prohibition, He tested them with what He adorned for them of the world and with the desires He placed within them. The former is a test by His law and command, and the latter is a test by His decree and destiny (qadar). Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾.

And He said: ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 22, verse 73:

Those who associate with Him others in worship have not measured God with His true measure. They worship what cannot create the weakest and smallest of creatures, and if a fly were to snatch away from them anything that is upon them, they would not be able to rescue it from it. And God, Exalted, said: ﴿They have not measured God with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate.﴾ [al-Zumar: 67] So whoever associates with Him in worship one who has no share of any of this whatsoever has not measured the One of such a state and greatness with His true measure. Rather, that (idol) is the most incapable and weakest of things. Thus, whoever associates with the Strong, the Mighty, one who is weak and humble has not measured the Strong and Mighty with His true measure.

(Benefit)

Reflect upon this parable, which all people are commanded to listen to, for whoever does not listen to it has disobeyed His command. Consider how it encompasses the refutation of polytheism and its causes, with the soundest proof, in the most concise, most eloquent, and sweetest expression. It also records against all the gods of the polytheists that, even if they all gathered in one place, helped one another, and assisted each other with the utmost assistance, they would be unable to create a single fly. Then it shows their weakness and incapacity to rescue what the fly snatches from them when it lands upon them. Which god is weaker than this sought god, and than his worshipper who seeks his benefit and goodness? Have they then measured the Strong, the Mighty, with His true measure, by associating with Him gods of this description?

Thus God established the proof of monotheism and exposed the falsehood of the people of polytheism and atheism with the sweetest and finest words, which no difficulty of obscurity has made hard, no lengthiness has blemished, no shortfall has marred, and no addition or deficiency has altered. Rather, they reached such beauty, eloquence, clarity, and conciseness that no one imagines, nor does anyone suppose, that anything could be more expressive of its meaning than them. And beneath them is a meaning of sublime worth, great honour, and far-reaching benefit that is greater than the words themselves.

(Section)

It is incumbent upon every servant to let his heart listen to this parable and to reflect upon it as it truly deserves, for it cuts off the sources of polytheism from the heart. This is because the least degree of a worshipped one is that it be able to bring into existence what benefits its worshipper and to bring about the removal of what harms him. Yet the gods that the polytheists worship besides God will not be able to create a fly, even if they all gathered together to create it. So how could they create what is greater than it?

Nor are they able to avenge themselves upon the fly when it snatches from them something of what is upon them, such as perfume or the like, so that they might rescue it from it. So they are neither able to create the fly, which is among the weakest of creatures, nor to avenge themselves upon it and retrieve what it has taken from them. There is no one more incapable than these gods, nor weaker than them. So how can any sensible person deem their worship besides God to be good?

This parable is among the most eloquent of what God, Glory be to Him, has sent down concerning the nullity of polytheism, the ignorance of its people, the condemnation of their minds, and the testimony that Satan has toyed with them more than children toy with a ball, in that they gave divinity, of whose necessary attributes is power over all that is possible, comprehensive knowledge of all that is known, independence from all creation, and to whom one turns in all needs, relief from distresses, aid in calamities, and answering of supplications, to images and statues which are incapable of even the least of the creatures belonging to the God of Truth, and the most humble, smallest and most contemptible of them, even if they gathered for that purpose and cooperated in it.

Even more indicative of their incapacity and the negation of their divinity is that if this creature, the least, most humble, incapable and weak, were to snatch something from them and carry it off, and they gathered together to rescue it from it, they would be unable to do so and would not be capable of it.

Then He equated the worshipper and the worshipped in weakness and incapacity by His saying: ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾

It has been said: the seeker is the worshipper and the sought is the worshipped, so one incapable is clinging to another incapable.

It has also been said: this is an equation between the one who seizes and the one who is seized, that is, an equation between the god and the fly in weakness and incapacity.

On this view, it has been said: the seeker is the false god, and the sought is the fly, which seeks from it what it has taken from it.

And it has been said: the seeker is the fly, and the sought is the god, for the fly seeks from it what it takes from what is upon them.

The correct view is that the expression encompasses all of these: the weakness of the worshipper and the worshipped, of the one who seizes and the one who is seized. Whoever makes such a thing a god alongside the Strong, the Mighty, has not measured Him with His true measure, nor known Him with His true knowledge, nor magnified Him with His true magnification.

(Benefit)

The places of prostration in the Qur'an are of two kinds: informative and imperative. The informative kind is a report from Allah Most High about the prostration of His creatures to Him, whether in general or in particular. So it is sunnah for the reciter and the listener, whether as an obligation or as a recommendation, to imitate them when reciting or hearing the verse of prostration. The verses of command are even more deserving of this. There is no difference in this between one command and another. How, then, would the command in His words, ﴿So prostrate yourselves to Allah and worship [Him]﴾ [al-Najm: 62], require prostration while the command in His words, ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate yourselves﴾, would not?

So the one who prostrates either imitates those who were reported about, or complies with what he was commanded. Under either assessment, it is sunnah for him to prostrate at the end of the Hajj just as it is sunnah for him to prostrate at its beginning. Since the sunnah equated between them, sound analogy and true reasoning equate between them too.

This prostration Allah and His Messenger legislated as an act of worship when reciting and hearing these verses, as a means of drawing near to Him, as submission to His greatness, and as humility before Him. The combination of bowing (ruku') with some of its verses confirms and strengthens this; it does not weaken or undermine it. And Allah is the One sought for help.

As for the words of Allah Most High, ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow﴾ [Al 'Imran: 43], it is not a place of prostration because it is a specific report about the words of the angels to a particular woman, that she should persist in worship of her Lord through devout obedience (qunut) and pray to Him with bowing and prostration. So it is a report of what the angels said to her, and an informing from Allah Most High to us that the angels said that to Mary.

Thus its context is different from the context of the verses of prostration.

As for the weak hadith, it is from the narration of Abu Qudamah, whose name is al-Harith ibn 'Ubayd. Imam Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "He is unstable in his narrations (mudtarib al-hadith)." Yahya said: "He is nothing." al-Nasa'i said: "He is not strong." al-Azdi said: "Weak." Ibn Hibban said: "It is not to be used as evidence when he is alone." I say: this hadith has been criticized, and this is the point of objection. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, witnessed the Prophet's (ﷺ) prostration in the Mufassal (the final surahs) in ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾ and ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾.

Muslim mentioned this in his Sahih, and he prostrated with him. Even if the report of Abu Qudamah were authentic, the report of Abu Hurayrah would have to be given precedence over it, because it is affirmative, so it carries additional knowledge. And Allah knows best.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in his commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 22, verse 78 (part 1 of 2):

God informed that He has chosen them (*ijtaba*, "to choose"). *Al-ijtiba'* is like *al-istifa'* (selection), and it is a form of *ifti'al* from *ijtaba al-shay'* (he gathered the thing), when one draws it to himself and takes it into his own possession. Thus, *al-mujtabun* (the chosen ones) are those whom God has drawn to Himself and made His people, His special ones, and His elite among His creation after the Prophets and Messengers. For this reason, He commanded them to strive for Him with the striving due to Him, by sacrificing themselves for Him, by singling Him out with love and worship, and by choosing Him alone as their God, the one worshipped and beloved above all else, just as He chose them over others. So they take Him alone as their God, their object of worship, the One they draw near to with their tongues, their limbs, their hearts, their love and their will. They prefer Him in every state over anyone else, just as He took them as His servants, His allies and His beloved, and preferred them over others by this.

Then He informed them that He made His religion easy for them to the utmost degree of ease, and did not place upon them any hardship whatsoever, out of the perfection of His love for them, His kindness, His mercy and His tenderness toward them. Then He commanded them to adhere to the religion (*millah*) of the Imam of the *hanifs* (those who turn away from falsehood to pure monotheism), their father Ibrahim (Abraham). It is the singling out of Him, exalted is He, alone, with worship, veneration, love, fear, hope, reliance, turning in repentance, entrusting, and submission. Thus the attachment of their hearts to that should be to Him alone and not to anything else. Then He informed that He has honoured them, named them thus after bringing them into existence, out of care for them, to elevate their station and to raise their rank.

Then He informed that He did this so that His Messenger would bear witness against them, and they would bear witness against the people. Thus they will be those for whom the Messenger's testimony is given, and they will be witnesses over the nations concerning the establishment of God's proof against them. So this honouring and this mention, with these two great matters and these two magnificent wisdoms, was made.

The point is that if they hold this status with Him, exalted is He, it is impossible that He would deprive all of them of the correct position on a matter, so that some of them give a wrong ruling on it while no one else gives the correct ruling, and that the guidance on it would be attained after them. And God is the One sought for help.

(Benefit)
The word ﴿مِلَّةَ﴾ (millata, "religion") is in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning "follow and adhere to" ﴿millata abikum﴾ ("the religion of your father"). What indicates the omitted verb is what preceded it, the words ﴿وَجاهِدُوا في اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهادِهِ﴾ ("and strive for God with the striving due to Him"). This is what is called *al-igra'* (urging or stirring up to an action).
It has also been said that it is in the accusative as an absolute object (*insab al-masadir*, the verbal noun construction), and the governing element is the sense of what came before it.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to instruct his companions that when they reached the morning and when they reached the evening, they should say: "We have risen upon the fitrah of Islam, the word of sincerity, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, and the religion of our father Ibrahim, a hanif, a Muslim, and he was not one of the polytheists."

Consider how these words make fitrah (innate disposition) belong to Islam, for it is the fitrah of God upon which He created mankind. The word of sincerity is the testimony that there is no god but God. The millah (religion) belongs to Ibrahim, for he is its possessor, and it is tawhid (monotheism) and the worship of God alone with no partner, and loving Him above every love. The din (way of life) belongs to the Prophet (ﷺ), and it is his complete religion and his perfect law, comprehensive of all of that. And He, glorified is He, named Ibrahim an imam (leader), an ummah (community), a qanit (devoutly obedient) and a hanif. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed I will make you a leader for the people. He said: And from my descendants? He said: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers.﴾

(Benefit)
God, exalted is He, says: ﴿He named you Muslims before this and in this﴾.
That is, God named you before the Qur'an and in the Qur'an. So God's naming them Muslims preceded their becoming Muslims and preceded their existence.

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And hold fast to God; He is your Protector, and what an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper﴾.
That is: whenever you hold fast to Him, He will take you as His ally, and He will help you against yourselves and against Satan. These are the two enemies that never leave the servant, and their enmity is more harmful than the enmity of an external enemy. So victory over this enemy is more important, and the servant is more in need of it. The perfection of victory over the enemy is proportionate to the perfection of holding fast to God.

(Section)
God commanded them to strive for Him with the striving due to Him, just as He commanded them to fear Him with the fear due to Him. Just as the fear due to Him is that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not disbelieved, so the striving due to Him is that the servant strive against his own self so that he submits his heart, his tongue and his limbs wholly to God, so that all of him belongs to God and is by God, not for himself and not by himself. He also strives against his Satan by denying his promise, disobeying his command, and committing what he forbids. For he promises false hopes and wishes for delusion, he promises poverty and commands indecency, and he forbids piety, guidance, chastity, patience and all the characteristics of faith. So strive against him by denying his promise and disobeying his command. From these two struggles there arises for him strength, authority and equipment, with which he strives against the enemies of God outwardly with his heart, his tongue, his hand and his wealth, so that the word of God may be supreme.

The expressions of the early generations (*salaf*) differed concerning the right of striving:
Ibn 'Abbas said: it is exhausting one's capacity in it, and that one does not fear the blame of any blamer in God's cause. Muqatil said: act for God with the right of His action, and worship Him with the right of His worship. 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: it is struggling against the self and desire. He who said that the two verses are abrogated (*mansukhatan*, by the principle of *naskh*, abrogation) was not correct, thinking that they include a command to what cannot be borne. The right of His fear and the right of His striving is what each servant is able to bear within himself, and this differs according to the differing states of the responsible persons in capacity and incapacity, knowledge and ignorance. So the right of piety and the right of striving in relation to the capable, empowered, knowledgeable person is one thing, and in relation to the incapable, ignorant, weak person is another. Consider how He followed the command with His saying: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].

The *haraj* (hardship) is narrowness. Rather, He made it wide, embracing everyone, just as He made His provision embrace every living being. He imposed upon the servant what the servant can bear, and gave the servant provision that suffices the servant. So His obligation is within what the servant can bear, and His provision is sufficient for him. He did not place upon His servant any hardship in the religion in any way whatsoever. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I was sent with the easy, tolerant hanifiyyah (the upright monotheistic path)." That is, with the religion; it is hanifiyyah in tawhid and samhah (tolerant) in practice.

God, glorified and exalted is He, has extended to His servants the utmost extent of expansiveness in His religion, His provision, His pardon and His forgiveness. He has spread out repentance for them as long as the soul is in the body, and has opened for them a door to it that He does not close to them until the sun rises from the west. He has made for every bad deed an expiation that erases it, through repentance, charity, a good deed that effaces it, or a calamity that expiates it. For everything He forbade them, He made a substitute from the lawful that is more beneficial, purer and more delicious for them, which takes its place, so that the servant may be independent of the forbidden and the lawful suffices him and does not constrict him. For every hardship with which He tests them, He made ease before it and ease after it. "Hardship will never overcome two eases." If this is His manner, glorified is He, with His servants, how would He impose upon them what does not suffice them, let alone what they cannot bear and have no power over?

(Another Section)
The more the servant draws near to God, the greater his striving for God becomes. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And strive for God with the striving due to Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 78].
Consider the states of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions. Whenever they advanced in nearness in a station, their striving and their effort grew greater. This is not like what some of the heretics (*malahidah*) who claim to be on the Path have supposed, when one of them said: "True nearness is the servant's movement from outward states to inward deeds, and it relieves the body and the limbs from the toil of action."

These people are greater in disbelief and heresy, for they have nullified servitude and thought they are independent of it because of the false imaginings that have come to them, which are among the wishes of the self and the deceptions of Satan. It is as if their speaker meant only himself and the adherents of his school when he said:

They were content with wishes, and were afflicted by their portions,
And they plunged into the seas of love by claim, but were not wetted.

They in the night journey have not left their place,
And they did not move away from it in the journey, though they became weary.

The people of uprightness and the imams of the Path have explicitly declared these people to be disbelievers, and have expelled them from Islam. They said: "Even if the servant reaches the highest station of nearness that a servant can attain, not a mustard seed's weight of the obligation falls from him, as long as he is able to fulfil it."
These people suppose that by this reality they become independent of the outward Shari'ah (sacred law).
This group has unanimously agreed that this is disbelief and heresy, and they have stated explicitly that every reality not followed by a Shari'ah is disbelief.

Sari al-Saqati said: "Whoever claims the inner reality, while the outer ruling nullifies it, is mistaken." Sayyid al-Ta'ifah (the leader of the group) al-Junayd ibn Muhammad said: "Our knowledge is interlaced with the hadith of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Nasrabadhi said: "The origin of this path is constant adherence to the Book and the Sunnah, abandoning desires and innovations, holding fast to the imams, following the early generations, and leaving what the later ones have introduced, and remaining upon what the first ones followed."

Isma'il ibn Nujayd was asked: "What is it that the servant cannot do without?" He said: "Constant adherence to servitude upon the Sunnah, and continuous vigilance (*muraqabah*, awareness of God)." He was asked: "What is tasawwuf (Sufism)?" He said: "Patience under the command and the prohibition."

Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari said: "Whoever acts without following the Sunnah, his action is void."

Al-Shibli said one day, extending his hand to his garment: "Were it not that it is borrowed, I would tear it." It was said to him: "Do you, in that state of overpowering, see your garments and that they are borrowed?" He said: "Yes. The people of realities (*arbab al-haqa'iq*) are always preserved by the Shari'ah at all times."

Abu Yazid al-Bistami said: "If you see a man who is given wondrous gifts (*karamat*) to the point that he rises into the air, do not be deceived by him until you look at how you find him at the command and the prohibition, and in the preservation of the limits and the Shari'ah."

'Abdullah al-Khayyat said: "People before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were governed by whatever occurred in their hearts. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) came and returned them from the heart to the religion and the Shari'ah."

When Abu 'Uthman al-Hiri was near death, his son Abu Bakr tore his shirt. Abu 'Uthman opened his eyes and said: "My son, opposition to the Sunnah in outward appearance is from the hypocrisy (*riya'*) of the inner heart."

Among the sayings of Ibn 'Uthman is this: "The safest of paths from delusion is the path of the early generations and adherence to the Shari'ah."

'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: "No light of faith appears upon anyone except by following the Sunnah and keeping away from innovation."

Every place where you see apparent striving without light, know that there is a hidden innovation there.

Sahl ibn 'Abdullah said: "Adhere to the black upon the white" (narrated and related to us) "if you wish to prosper."

The leaders of the group were at their most diligent in the last part of their lives.

Al-Qushayri said: I heard Abu 'Ali al-Daqqaq say: "A prayer-beads (*subhah*) was seen in al-Junayd's hand. It was said to him: 'You, with your nobility, take a prayer-beads in your hand?' He said: 'A path by which I reached my Lord, blessed and exalted is He, I will never leave, ever.'"

Isma'il ibn Nujayd said: "Al-Junayd used to come every day to the market, open the door of his shop, enter it, let down the curtain, pray four hundred rak'ahs, and then return to his house. Ibn 'Ata' entered upon him while he was in the throes of death, and greeted him. He did not return the greeting. Then after an hour he returned the greeting, and said: 'Excuse me, for I was in my litany (*wird*).' Then he turned his face toward the qiblah, said takbir, and died."

Abu Sa'id ibn al-A'rabi said: I heard Abu Bakr al-'Attar say: "I was present with Abu al-Qasim al-Junayd, I and a group of our companions. He was sitting praying, and when he wanted to prostrate he would fold his leg. He continued like that until the soul left his legs. Their movement became heavy for him, for they had swollen."
One of his companions said to him: "What is this, Abu al-Qasim?"
He said: "These are the blessings of God. God is greatest."
When he finished his prayer, Abu Muhammad al-Jaririy said to him: "Abu al-Qasim, if only you lay down."
He said: "Abu Muhammad, is this a time for that? God is greatest." His state remained so until he died.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 22, verse 78 (part 2 of 2):

A young man entered upon him (al-Junayd) during the illness in which he died, when his face had swollen. Before him was a pillow he was praying toward. The young man said: "At this hour you still do not abandon the prayer?" When he had finished the prayer, al-Junayd called him and said: "It is something through which I have reached Allah, so I will not abandon it." He died an hour later. May Allah have mercy on him.

Abu Muhammad al-Jurayri said: "I was standing at the head of al-Junayd at the time of his death. It was a Friday and the day of Nayruz (the Persian New Year festival), and he was reciting the Qur'an. I said to him: 'O Abu al-Qasim, be gentle with yourself.' He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, have you seen anyone more in need of it than I am at a time like this, when my record is being folded up?'"

Abu Bakr al-Atawi said: "I was with al-Junayd when he died. He completed the recitation of the Qur'an, then began another recitation. He recited seventy verses of al-Baqarah, and then he died."

Muhammad ibn Ibrahim said: "I saw al-Junayd in a dream and asked him: 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'Those allusions have perished, those expressions have vanished, those sciences have passed away, and those traces have been exhausted. Nothing benefited us except the rak'ahs we used to perform in the hours before dawn.'"

They discussed in his presence the people of gnosis (ma'rifah) and whether they had dismissed the litanies (awrad) and acts of worship after they had attained that station. Al-Junayd said: "Worship for the gnostics is better than crowns upon the heads of kings."

He also said: "All the paths are closed to creation, except for the one who follows the footsteps of the Messenger (ﷺ), adheres to his Sunnah (the Prophet's practice) and holds to his way. For the paths of all good are open to him." He also said: "Whoever thinks he will arrive by exerting his effort is toiling in vain, and whoever thinks he will arrive without exerting effort is merely wishing."

Abu Nu'aym said: "I heard my father say: I heard Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hani' say: I asked al-Junayd, 'What is the sign of faith?' He said: 'Its sign is obedience to the One in whom you believe, acting by what He loves and is pleased with, and leaving off preoccupation with what passes away and perishes.'"

So may Allah have mercy on Abu al-Qasim al-Junayd, and may Allah be pleased with him. How closely he followed the Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ), and how faithfully he followed the way of his Companions!

This is a subject whose tracing out would take a very long time.

It shows that people of uprightness (istiqamah) at the end of their path strive harder than they did at the beginning. Rather, their striving at the beginning was directed at a specific act, but at the end their striving became absolute obedience, and their will revolved around it. Thus their striving toward a particular matter weakens, because it had been divided between it and other things.

Nor should you give ear to the words of a heretic who cuts off the road, dressed in the garb of a gnostic, who says: "The station of nearness (qurb) transfers the servant from outward acts to inward acts, leads him to disdain the outward acts of obedience, and relieves him of the toil of performing them."

[Section: On the Levels of Jihad]

Having understood this, jihad has four levels: jihad against the self (nafs), jihad against Satan, jihad against the disbelievers, and jihad against the hypocrites.

The jihad against the self also has four levels:

The first: to strive against it in learning the guidance and the religion of truth, without which it has no success and no happiness in its life or its return. If it misses knowledge of this, it is wretched in both abodes.

The second: to strive against it in acting upon that knowledge after learning it. Otherwise, mere knowledge without action, if it does not harm the one who has it, does not benefit him.

The third: to strive against it in calling others to this, and teaching it to those who do not know. Otherwise, one is among those who conceal what Allah has sent down of guidance and clear proofs, and his knowledge will not benefit him, nor will it save him from the punishment of Allah.

The fourth: to strive against it in patience over the hardships of calling to Allah and the harm inflicted by people, and to bear all of that for the sake of Allah. When he completes these four levels, he becomes one of the rabbaniyyin (those devoted to the Lord, i.e., the godly scholars), for the early scholars (salaf) are unanimous that a scholar does not deserve to be called rabbani until he knows the truth, acts upon it, and teaches it. Whoever knows, acts, and teaches is the one who is called great in the kingdom of the heavens.

[Section: On the Levels of Jihad against Satan]

As for jihad against Satan, it has two levels. The first is striving to repel the doubts and misgivings that he casts upon the servant, which undermine faith.

The second is striving to repel the corrupt desires and appetites that he casts toward him. The first kind of jihad is followed by certainty (yaqin), and the second is followed by patience (sabr). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We appointed from among them leaders guiding by Our command, when they were patient and were certain of Our signs﴾ [As-Sajdah: 24].

So He informed that leadership in the religion is attained only through patience and certainty. Patience repels the appetites and corrupt desires, and certainty repels doubts and misgivings.

[Section: On the Levels of Jihad against the Disbelievers and Hypocrites]

As for jihad against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, it has four levels: with the heart, the tongue, wealth, and the self. Jihad against the disbelievers is especially by the hand, and jihad against the hypocrites is especially by the tongue.

[Section: On the Jihad of the Lords of Oppression, Innovation and Evils]

As for jihad against the lords of oppression, innovation, and evil deeds, it has three levels. The first is by the hand, if one is able. If one is unable, he moves to the tongue. If he is unable, he strives with his heart. So these are thirteen levels of jihad. And the hadith: "Whoever dies without having fought, and without having resolved in his soul to fight, dies upon a branch of hypocrisy."

[Section: On the Condition of Jihad]

Jihad is not complete except with emigration (hijrah), and neither emigration nor jihad is complete except with faith. Those who hope for the mercy of Allah are those who have fulfilled these three. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who emigrated and strove in the way of Allah, those hope for the mercy of Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 218].

Just as faith is obligatory upon every person, two emigrations are obligatory upon him at all times: an emigration to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through monotheism, sincerity, turning back in repentance, reliance, fear, hope, love, and repentance; and an emigration to His Messenger by following him, submitting to his command, affirming his report, and giving precedence to his command and report over the command and report of others. The hadith says: "Whoever's emigration was to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's emigration was to a worldly gain he may acquire or a woman he may marry, his emigration is to what he emigrated for." He also obligated upon him jihad against his own self for the sake of Allah, and jihad against his Satan. All of this is an individual obligation (fard 'ayn) for which no one can substitute another.

As for jihad against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, it may be sufficient that some of the community perform it, if the purpose of jihad is achieved by them.

[Section: The Third Degree: Allah Choosing His Servant]

He said: "The third degree: the choosing (ijtiba') of the servant by the Truth, and His selecting him for Himself with His own essence, just as He began with Musa, when he went out seeking a fire, and He chose him for Himself, and left from him a borrowed trace."

I say: al-ijtiba' is the selection, preference, and singling out. It is an iftial form from jaba'tu al-shay', when you gather and secure something to yourself, like the collection of taxes and other things.

Al-istina' is also selection and choosing; it means that He selected Musa and chose him for Himself.

He made him purely His own without any cause from Musa or any means. He went out to seek fire, and returned as the interlocutor of the One, the Subduer. He became the most honored of creation before Him, beginning from Him, glory be to Him, without any prior merit or any preceding means. Concerning this it has been said:

"O servant, be for what you do not hope for
of goodness, more hopeful than what you hope for.
Indeed Musa came to seek a fire
from a light he saw while the night was dark.
He turned back, and Allah had spoken to him,
and He conversed with him, and He is the best of interlocutors."

As for his saying: "and left from him a borrowed trace."

It may be understood that by the trace he means the remnant by which Muhammad (ﷺ) surpassed him, and he was raised above him by degrees because of its remaining from him.

And it may also be understood, and this is the more apparent, that He took him from himself, made him for Himself, chose him from among the worlds, singled him out with His speech, and left for him from himself only a bare trace by which he accompanies creation, and upon which the rulings of human nature apply, completing His wisdom and manifesting His power. So it is a loan with Him. When He has fulfilled what is upon him, He takes back that trace and makes it part of His property. Then the station of choosing is perfected, outwardly and inwardly, in reality and in form, and the loan returns to its true owner, to whom the whole matter returns. Thus, as it began from Him, it returns to Him.

Musa (peace be upon him) was in the aspect of majesty (jalal), and for this reason his law was a law of majesty and subjugation. They were commanded to kill their own selves, fats were forbidden to them, as were animals with claws and other good things, and spoils of war were forbidden to them. Punishments were hastened upon them, and they were burdened with heavy obligations and shackles that no one else was burdened with.

Musa (ﷺ) was among the greatest of Allah's creation in awe and dignity, and in the strength of his might and his anger for Allah, and in seizing the enemies of Allah. No one could bear to look at him.

Isa (peace be upon him) was in the aspect of beauty (jamal). His law was a law of grace and kindness. He did not fight or wage war, and there is no fighting at all in his law. The Christians are forbidden by their religion from fighting, and in doing so they disobey his law. The Gospel commands them: whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him your left cheek; whoever takes your cloak, give him your outer garment; whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two miles; and similar things. There is no hardship in their law, no heavy burdens, and no shackles. The Christians themselves invented that monasticism (rahbaniyyah) on their own initiative, and it was not prescribed for them.

As for our Prophet (ﷺ): he was in the aspect of perfection, combining that strength, justice, and severity in the cause of Allah, with this gentleness, compassion, and mercy. His law is the most perfect of laws. He is the Prophet of perfection, his law is the law of perfection, and his community is the most perfect of communities. Their conditions and stations are the most perfect of conditions and stations.

For this reason his law brings justice as an obligation and a duty, and grace as a recommendation and a desirable matter. It brings severity in the place of severity and gentleness in the place of gentleness. The sword was placed in its place, and generosity was placed in its place. So it mentions injustice and forbids it, and justice and makes it obligatory, and grace and recommends it, in various verses.

Like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [Ash-Shura: 40], this is justice. ﴿But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura: 40], this is grace. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾ [Ash-Shura: 40], this is a prohibition of injustice. And His saying: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾ [An-Nahl: 126], this is an obligation of justice and a prohibition of injustice. ﴿But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ [An-Nahl: 126], this recommends grace. And His saying: ﴿And if you repent, you will have your principal, neither wronging nor being wronged﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 279], a prohibition of injustice. ﴿And if someone is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 280], this is justice. ﴿But that you give charity is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 280], this is grace.

Likewise is the prohibition of what He prohibited for his community, as protection and safeguarding. He forbade them every corrupt and harmful thing, and permitted for them every good and beneficial thing. So its prohibition for them is mercy, and for those before them it was not free of punishment. He guided them to what the nations before them had strayed from. He bestowed upon them some of His knowledge and forbearance. He made them the best community brought forth for mankind. He perfected for them the excellences that He had distributed among the nations before them, just as He perfected for their Prophet (ﷺ) the excellences He had distributed among the prophets before him. He perfected in His Book the excellences that He had distributed among the books before it, and likewise in His law.

These are the cherished ones (al-dana'in), the chosen and the best, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78]. He also made them witnesses over mankind, and established them in that station as the prophets who bear witness over their nations.

The detailed explanation of the excellence of this community and its distinctive features would require a book, indeed many books. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
